1.Expressive Whole-Body Control for Humanoid Robots
人形机器人富有表现力的全身控制
为了能够让类人机器人在现实世界中产生丰富、多样且富有表现力的动作，人们通常会在强化学习框架中利用来自图形社区的大规模人体动作捕捉数据。 然而，考虑到自由度和物理能力的巨大差距，直接使用动作捕捉数据集进行模仿学习在真正的人形机器人上是行不通的。
来自加州大学圣地亚哥分校的学者们提出了一种方法——表达性全身控制（ExBody），通过鼓励上半身模仿参考运动，同时放松对两条腿的模仿约束，只要求它们稳健地遵循给定的速度。 通过模拟实验和 Sim2Real 迁移训练，学者们的策略可以控制人形机器人以不同的方式行走，与人类握手，甚至与现实世界中的人类跳舞。学者们对模拟和现实世界中的各种运动进行了广泛的研究和比较，以证明了他们方法的有效性。
To enable humanoid robots to produce rich, diverse, and expressive movements in the real world, large-scale human motion capture data from the graphics community are often leveraged in reinforcement learning frameworks. However, considering the huge gap in degrees of freedom and physical capabilities, directly using motion capture datasets for imitation learning is not feasible on real humanoid robots.
Expressive Whole Body Control (ExBody), a method proposed by scholars from the University of California, San Diego, solves this problem by encouraging the upper body to imitate the reference movement while relaxing the imitation constraints on the two legs and only requiring them to robustly follow a given speed. . Trained through simulation and Sim2Real transfer, Scholar's strategy can control humanoid robots to walk in different ways, shake hands with humans, and even dance with real-world humans. Scholars have conducted extensive research and comparisons on various motions in simulations and the real world to demonstrate the effectiveness of their methods.
2.Learning Human-to-Humanoid Real-Time Whole-Body Teleoperation
学习人对人的实时全身远程操作
来自卡内基梅隆大学的学者们推出了 Human to Humanoid (H2O)，这是一种基于强化学习 (RL) 的框架，可仅通过 RGB 摄像头对全尺寸人形机器人进行实时全身远程操作。 为了为仿人机器人创建大规模的人体运动重定向运动数据集，学者们们提出了一种可扩展的“模拟到数据”过程，使用特权运动模仿器来过滤和选择可行的运动。 然后，他们使用这些精细的运动在模拟中训练一个强大的实时人形运动模仿器，并以零样本的方式将其传输到真正的人形机器人。学者们们成功实现了现实场景中动态全身运动的远程操作，包括行走、后跳、踢腿、转身、挥手、推、拳击等。据他们所知，这是第一个实现学习的演示—— 基于实时全身人形遥控操作。
Academics from Carnegie Mellon University have introduced Human to Humanoid (H2O), a reinforcement learning (RL)-based framework for real-time, whole-body teleoperation of full-scale humanoid robots using only RGB cameras. To create a large-scale human motion retargeting motion dataset for humanoid robots, scholars propose a scalable “simulation-to-data” process that uses privileged motion imitators to filter and select feasible motions. They then used these fine-scale movements to train a powerful real-time humanoid motion emulator in simulation and transferred it to a real humanoid robot in a zero-shot manner. Scholars have successfully achieved remote operation of dynamic whole-body movements in real-life scenarios, including walking, jumping back, kicking, turning, waving, pushing, boxing, etc. To their knowledge, this is the first demonstration of learning based on real-time full-body humanoid remote control.
3.HumanoidBench: Simulated Humanoid Benchmark for Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation
HumanoidBench ：用于全身运动和操纵的模拟人形基准
人形机器人由于其利用类人形态的灵活性和适应性，在帮助人类完成不同环境和任务方面有着巨大的前景。 然而，人形机器人的研究常常受到昂贵且脆弱的硬件设置的瓶颈。 为了加速人形机器人的算法研究，来自加州大学伯克利分校和延世大学的学者们提出了一个高维模拟机器人学习基准HumanoidBench，其特点是人形机器人配备灵巧的双手和各种具有挑战性的全身操纵和运动任务。 学者们的研究结果表明，最先进的强化学习算法很难完成大多数任务，而分层学习基线在强大的低级策略（例如行走或伸手）的支持下可以实现卓越的性能。 通过HumanoidBench，学者们为机器人社区提供了一个平台，以识别使用人形机器人解决各种任务时出现的挑战，促进算法和想法的及时验证。
Humanoid robots hold great promise in helping humans complete different environments and tasks due to their flexibility and adaptability in utilizing humanoid forms. However, research on humanoid robots is often bottlenecked by expensive and fragile hardware setups. To accelerate algorithm research on humanoid robots, scholars from the University of California, Berkeley, and Yonsei University proposed HumanoidBench, a high-dimensional simulation robot learning benchmark that features humanoid robots equipped with dexterous hands and a variety of challenging full-body manipulations and movements. Task. The academics' results show that state-of-the-art reinforcement learning algorithms struggle to complete most tasks, while hierarchical learning baselines can achieve superior performance when supported by powerful low-level strategies such as walking or reaching. Through HumanoidBench, academics provide the robotics community with a platform to identify challenges that arise when using humanoid robots to solve various tasks, facilitating the timely verification of algorithms and ideas.
4.Humanoid Parkour Learning
人形跑酷学习
跑酷对于腿部运动来说是一个巨大的挑战，甚至对于四足机器人来说也是如此，它需要主动感知和各种动作来克服多个具有挑战性的障碍。现有的人形运动方法要么优化单个跑酷赛道的轨迹，要么训练强化学习策略 ，只在有大量运动参考的情况下行走。
在这项工作中，来自上海科技大学 和MARS Lab的学者们提出了一个框架，用于学习端到端基于视觉的全身控制跑酷策略，用于人形机器人，该策略可以在没有任何运动先验的情况下克服多种跑酷技能。使用跑酷策略，人形机器人可以跳上 0.42 米的平台，跳过障碍物、0.8 米的间隙等等。它还可以在野外以 1.8 米/秒的速度奔跑，并在不同的地形上稳健行走。学者们在室内和室外环境中测试了我们的策略，以证明它可以在遵循操纵杆的旋转命令的同时自主选择跑酷技能。学者们的试验覆盖了手臂动作，并表明该框架可以轻松转移到人形移动操纵任务。
Parkour is a huge challenge for legged locomotion, even for quadruped robots, requiring active perception and a variety of actions to overcome multiple challenging obstacles. Existing humanoid locomotion methods either optimize the trajectory of a single parkour track or train a reinforcement learning policy that only walks with a large number of motion references.
In this work, scholars from ShanghaiTech University and MARS Lab propose a framework for learning an end-to-end vision-based full-body control parkour policy for a humanoid robot that can overcome multiple parkour skills without any motion priors. Using the parkour policy, the humanoid robot can jump onto a 0.42-meter platform, jump over obstacles, 0.8-meter gaps, and more. It can also run at a speed of 1.8 m/s in the wild and walk robustly on different terrains. Scholars tested our policy in indoor and outdoor environments to demonstrate that it can autonomously select parkour skills while following the rotation commands of the joystick. Scholars' experiments cover arm movements and show that the framework can be easily transferred to humanoid mobile manipulation tasks.
OmniH2O: Universal and Dexterous Human-toHumanoid Whole-Body Teleoperation and Learning
OmniH2O：通用灵巧的人机全身远程操作和学习
来自卡内基梅隆大学和上海交通大学的学者们推出了 OmniH2O（Omni Human-to-Humanoid），这是一种基于学习的全身人形机器人远程操作和自主系统。OmniH2O 使用运动姿势作为通用控制界面，使人类能够以各种方式控制具有灵巧双手的全尺寸人形机器人，包括通过 VR 耳机、口头指令和 RGB 摄像头进行实时远程操作。OmniH2O 还通过从远程操作演示中学习或与 GPT-4 等前沿模型集成来实现完全自主。OmniH2O 通过远程操作或自主展示了各种现实世界全身任务的多功能性和灵活性，例如进行多种运动、移动和操纵物体以及与人类互动。学者们开发了基于 RL 的模拟到现实管道，其中包括大规模重新定位和增强人体运动数据集，通过模仿特权教师策略学习具有稀疏传感器输入的真实世界可部署策略，以及奖励设计以增强鲁棒性和稳定性。他们发布了第一个人形全身控制数据集 OmniH2O-6，包含六项日常任务，并展示了从遥控数据集进行的人形全身技能学习。
Scholars from Carnegie Mellon University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University present OmniH2O (Omni Human-to-Humanoid), a learning-based full-body humanoid teleoperation and autonomy system. OmniH2O uses motion gestures as a universal control interface to enable humans to control a full-size humanoid robot with dexterous hands in a variety of ways, including real-time teleoperation via VR headsets, verbal commands, and RGB cameras. OmniH2O also achieves full autonomy by learning from teleoperation demonstrations or integrating with cutting-edge models such as GPT-4. OmniH2O demonstrates versatility and flexibility for a variety of real-world full-body tasks, such as performing multiple movements, moving and manipulating objects, and interacting with humans, either through teleoperation or autonomy. The scholars develop an RL-based simulation-to-reality pipeline that includes a large-scale relocalization and augmentation of human motion datasets, learning real-world deployable policies with sparse sensor inputs by imitating privileged teacher policies, and reward design to enhance robustness and stability. They released the first humanoid full-body control dataset, OmniH2O-6, containing six everyday tasks, and demonstrated humanoid full-body skill learning from a teleoperation dataset.
HumanPlus: Humanoid Shadowing and Imitation from Humans
HumanPlus：人形机器人跟踪和模仿人类
制造与人类外形相似的机器人的关键论点之一是人们可以利用大量人类数据进行训练。然而，由于人形机器人感知和控制的复杂性、形态和驱动方面的人形机器人与人类之间存在的物理差距以及人形机器人缺乏从自我中心视觉学习自主技能的数据管道，因此在实践中这样做仍然具有挑战性。
在本文中，来自斯坦福大学的学者们介绍了一个全栈系统，供人形机器人从人类数据中学习运动和自主技能。学者们首先使用现有的 40 小时人体运动数据集通过强化学习在模拟中训练低级策略。该策略转移到现实世界，并允许人形机器人仅使用 RGB 摄像头（即阴影）实时跟踪人体和手部运动。通过阴影，操作员可以远程操作人形机器人以收集全身数据，以学习现实世界中的不同任务。然后，学者们使用收集到的数据进行监督行为克隆，以使用自我中心视觉训练技能策略，使人形机器人能够通过模仿人类技能自主完成不同的任务。我们在定制的 33-DoF 180 厘米人形机器人上演示了该系统，通过多达 40 次演示，该机器人可以自主完成穿鞋站立和行走、从仓库货架上卸下物品、折叠运动衫、重新排列物品、打字和迎接另一个机器人等任务，成功率达到 60-100％。
One of the key arguments for making robots that resemble humans is that one can leverage a large amount of human data for training. However, doing so in practice remains challenging due to the complexity of humanoid perception and control, the physical gap between humanoids and humans in terms of morphology and actuation, and the lack of a data pipeline for humanoids to learn autonomous skills from egocentric vision.
In this paper, scholars from Stanford University introduce a full-stack system for humanoid robots to learn motion and autonomous skills from human data. The scholars first use an existing 40-hour human motion dataset to train a low-level policy in simulation via reinforcement learning. The policy transfers to the real world and allows the humanoid robot to track human and hand motions in real time using only an RGB camera (i.e., shadows). With shadows, operators can teleoperate the humanoid robot to collect full-body data to learn different tasks in the real world. The scholars then use the collected data for supervised behavior cloning to train a skill policy using egocentric vision, enabling the humanoid robot to autonomously complete different tasks by mimicking human skills. We demonstrate the system on a custom-built 33-DoF 180 cm humanoid robot that can autonomously complete tasks such as standing and walking with shoes on, unloading items from a warehouse shelf, folding a sweatshirt, rearranging items, typing, and greeting another robot with a success rate of 60-100% over up to 40 demonstrations.
Blind Walking Balance Control and Disturbance Rejection of the Bipedal Humanoid Robot Xiao-Man via Reinforcement Learning
基于强化学习的双足人形机器人小蛮盲行平衡控制与干扰抑制
双足仿人机器人具备在复杂环境下移动和操控的能力，在未来具有重要意义。然而，在现实世界中实现双足稳定行走一直是工业界乃至学术界面临的挑战。传统的基于模型的方法对环境依赖性强，建模复杂度高，泛化能力不足。基于简化模型的解决方案通常会导致控制算法无法适应复杂地形环境的问题。
本文介绍了一种新型双足仿人机器人。为了实现机器人的地形自适应行走行为，来自中科大的学者们提出了一种基于强化学习的非对称结构Actor-Critic网络。在不使用任何外部感知信息的情况下，小蛮实现了稳健的双足行走行为。在此过程中，学者们还基于关节驱动真实数据构建数据集，并训练关节执行器网络以减少期望力矩与实际响应力矩之间的差距。实验结果表明，配备训练好的控制策略的双足仿人机器人仅依靠本体感受信息即可实现稳定行走和抗干扰的能力。
Bipedal humanoid robots have the ability to move and manipulate in complex environments, which is of great significance in the future. However, achieving stable bipedal walking in the real world has always been a challenge faced by industry and even academia. Traditional model-based methods are highly dependent on the environment, have high modeling complexity, and lack generalization ability. Solutions based on simplified models usually lead to the problem that the control algorithm cannot adapt to complex terrain environments.
This paper introduces a new type of bipedal humanoid robot. In order to achieve terrain-adaptive walking behavior of the robot, scholars from the University of Science and Technology of China proposed an asymmetric structure Actor-Critic network based on reinforcement learning. Without using any external perception information, Xiaoman achieved robust bipedal walking behavior. In the process, scholars also constructed a dataset based on real joint drive data and trained the joint actuator network to reduce the gap between the expected torque and the actual response torque. The experimental results show that the bipedal humanoid robot equipped with a trained control strategy can achieve stable walking and anti-interference capabilities relying only on proprioceptive information.
WoCoCo: Learning Whole-Body Humanoid Control with Sequential Contacts    WoCoCo：通过顺序接触学习全身人形机器人控制
涉及顺序接触的类人机器人活动对于现实世界中复杂的机器人交互和操作至关重要，传统上通过基于模型的运动规划来解决，这非常耗时，并且通常依赖于简化的动力学模型。尽管无模型强化学习 (RL) 已成为多功能、强大的全身类人机器人控制的强大工具，但它仍然需要繁琐的任务特定调整和状态机设计，并且在涉及接触序列的任务中存在长期探索问题。
在这项工作中，来自卡内基梅隆大学的学者们提出了 WoCoCo（具有顺序接触的全身控制），这是一个统一的框架，通过将任务自然分解为单独的接触阶段来学习具有顺序接触的全身类人机器人控制。这种分解通过与任务无关的奖励和模拟到现实设计促进了简单而通用的策略学习管道，只需要为每个任务指定一个或两个与任务相关的术语。学者们证明了使用 WoCoCo 训练的端到端 RL 控制器能够完成四项具有挑战性的全身类人机器人任务，这些任务涉及现实世界中的各种接触序列，且无需任何运动先验：1) 多功能跑酷跳跃、2) 箱式机器人操控、3) 动态拍手和踢踏舞以及 4) 悬崖攀爬。他们进一步证明了 WoCoCo 是一个超越类人机器人的通用框架，它应用于 22 自由度恐龙机器人操控任务。
Humanoid robot activities involving sequential contact are critical for complex robotic interactions and manipulation in the real world and are traditionally addressed via model-based motion planning, which is time-consuming and often relies on simplified dynamics models. While model-free reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful tool for versatile, robust full-body humanoid robot control, it still requires tedious task-specific tuning and state machine design, and has long-standing exploration issues in tasks involving contact sequences.
In this work, scholars from Carnegie Mellon University propose WoCoCo (Whole-Body Control with Sequential Contact), a unified framework for learning full-body humanoid robot control with sequential contact by naturally decomposing the task into separate contact phases. This decomposition facilitates a simple and general policy learning pipeline through task-agnostic rewards and simulation-to-reality design, requiring only one or two task-related terms to be specified for each task. The researchers demonstrated that an end-to-end RL controller trained with WoCoCo is capable of completing four challenging full-body humanoid robotics tasks involving various contact sequences in the real world without any motion priors: 1) versatile parkour jumping, 2) box robot manipulation, 3) dynamic clapping and tap dancing, and 4) cliff climbing. They further demonstrated that WoCoCo is a general framework beyond humanoid robotics by applying it to a 22-DOF dinosaur robot manipulation task.
9.Open-TeleVision: Teleoperation with Immersive Active Visual Feedback
Open-TeleVision：具有沉浸式主动视觉反馈的远程操作
远程操作是一种从演示中收集机器人学习所需机器人数据的有效方法。远程操作系统的直观性和易用性对于确保高质量、多样化和可扩展的数据至关重要。
为了实现这一点，加州大学圣地亚哥分校和麻省理工学院的学者提出了一种沉浸式远程操作系统Open-TeleVision，该系统允许操作员以立体的方式主动感知机器人的周围环境。此外，该系统将操作员的手臂和手部动作镜像到机器人上，创造出一种身临其境的体验，就好像操作员的思想被传送到了机器人身上。学者们通过为2个不同的人形机器人收集数据，并为4个长期精确任务（罐头分类、罐头插入、折叠和卸载）训练模仿学习策略，并将其部署到现实世界中，验证了他们系统的有效性。
Teleoperation is a powerful method to collect robotic data necessary for robot learning from demonstrations. The intuitiveness and ease of use of the teleoperation system are critical to ensuring high-quality, diverse, and scalable data.
To achieve this, scholars from the University of California, San Diego and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology proposed an immersive teleoperation system, Open-TeleVision, which allows the operator to actively perceive the robot's surroundings in a stereoscopic manner. In addition, the system mirrors the operator's arm and hand movements on the robot, creating an immersive experience, as if the operator's thoughts were teleported to the robot. The scholars verified the effectiveness of their system by collecting data for 2 different humanoid robots and training imitation learning policies for four long-term precision tasks (can sorting, can insertion, folding, and unloading), and deployed them into the real world.
10.Design and Control of a Bipedal Robotic Character
双足机器人角色设计与控制
腿式机器人在具有挑战性的非结构化地形中取得了令人印象深刻的动态运动成就。然而，在娱乐应用中，这些机器人的设计和控制在吸引人类观众方面面临着额外的挑战。这项工作旨在统一腿式机器人富有表现力、艺术指导的运动和强大的动态移动性。为此，来自瑞士迪士尼研究中心和美国迪士尼研究中心的学者们提出了一种新型双足机器人，其设计侧重于角色驱动的机械性能。他们提出了一种基于强化学习的控制架构，以稳健地执行以命令信号为条件的艺术运动。在运行时，这些命令信号由动画引擎生成，该引擎在多个动画源之间进行合成和混合。最后，直观的操作员界面可以实时演示机器人的性能。完整的系统产生了一个可信的机器人角色，并为娱乐机器人和其他领域增强人机交互铺平了道路。
Legged robots have achieved impressive dynamic locomotion achievements in challenging unstructured terrain. However, in entertainment applications, the design and control of these robots face additional challenges in engaging human audiences. This work aims to unify expressive, artistically directed locomotion and robust dynamic mobility for legged robots. To this end, scholars from Disney Research Switzerland and Disney Research USA present a new bipedal robot whose design focuses on character-driven mechanical performance. They propose a reinforcement learning-based control architecture to robustly execute artistic locomotion conditioned on command signals. At runtime, these command signals are generated by an animation engine that synthesizes and blends between multiple animation sources. Finally, an intuitive operator interface enables real-time demonstration of the robot's performance. The complete system produces a believable robotic character and paves the way for enhanced human-robot interaction in entertainment robotics and other fields.
11.SkillMimic: Learning Reusable Basketball Skills from Demonstrations
SkillMimic：通过演示学习可重复使用的篮球技巧
掌握篮球技能（例如各种上篮和运球）涉及与球的复杂互动，需要实时调整。传统的互动技能强化学习方法依赖于劳动密集型、手动设计的奖励，这些奖励不能很好地推广到不同的技能。
受人类从演示中学习的启发，来自香港科技大学和清华大学以及卡内基梅隆大学的学者们提出了 SkillMimic，这是一种数据驱动的方法，可以模仿人类和球的运动来学习各种各样的篮球技能。SkillMimic 采用统一的配置从人球运动数据集中学习各种技能，随着数据集的增长，技能多样性和泛化能力不断提高。这种方法允许训练单一策略来学习多种技能，即使这些切换不存在于参考数据集中，也可以实现平稳的技能切换。SkillMimic 获得的技能可以被高级控制器轻松重用，以完成复杂的篮球任务。
为了评估这一方法，学者们引入了两个篮球数据集：一个是通过单目 RGB 视频估计的，另一个是使用先进的动作捕捉设备估计的，总共包含大约 35 分钟的各种篮球技能。实验表明，我们的方法可以有效地学习数据集中包含的所有篮球技能，并采用统一的配置，包括各种运球、上篮和投篮风格。此外，通过训练高级控制器来重用所学技能，我们可以实现复杂的篮球任务，例如得分，其中包括运球到篮筐、把握运球和上篮得分时机、抢篮板并重复该过程。
Mastering basketball skills, such as various layups and dribbles, involves complex interactions with the ball, requiring real-time adjustments. Traditional interactive skill reinforcement learning methods rely on labor-intensive, manually designed rewards that do not generalize well to different skills.
Inspired by how humans learn from demonstrations, scholars from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, as well as Carnegie Mellon University, proposed SkillMimic, a data-driven approach that imitates human and ball motion to learn a wide range of basketball skills. SkillMimic adopts a unified configuration to learn a wide range of skills from human-ball motion datasets, and the skill diversity and generalization ability continue to improve as the dataset grows. This approach allows a single policy to be trained to learn multiple skills, and enables smooth skill switching even if these switches are not present in the reference dataset. The skills acquired by SkillMimic can be easily reused by high-level controllers to complete complex basketball tasks.
To evaluate this method, the scholars introduced two basketball datasets: one estimated from monocular RGB videos and the other estimated using advanced motion capture equipment, containing a total of about 35 minutes of various basketball skills. Experiments show that our approach can effectively learn all basketball skills contained in the dataset in a uniform configuration, including various dribbling, layup, and shooting styles. Furthermore, by training a high-level controller to reuse the learned skills, we can achieve complex basketball tasks such as scoring, which involves dribbling to the basket, timing dribbling and layup, grabbing a rebound, and repeating the process.
12.ACE: A Cross-Platform Visual-Exoskeletons System for Low-Cost Dexterous Teleoperation
ACE：用于低成本灵巧遥控操作的跨平台视觉外骨骼系统
事实证明，从演示中学习是一种有效的机器人操作方法，尤其是最近收集的带有远程操作系统的大规模机器人数据。构建一个跨不同机器人平台的高效远程操作系统变得比以往任何时候都更加重要。然而，对于不同的终端执行器（例如，拟人化的机器人手和夹持器），明显缺乏经济高效且用户友好的远程操作系统，这些系统可以跨多个平台运行。
为了解决这个问题，来自加州大学圣地亚哥分校的学者们开发了 ACE，这是一种跨平台的视觉外骨骼系统，用于低成本的灵巧远程操作。学者们的系统利用面向手的摄像头捕捉 3D 手部姿势，并使用安装在便携式底座上的外骨骼，能够准确实时捕捉手指和手腕姿势。与以前的系统相比，以前的系统通常需要根据不同的机器人进行硬件定制，而他们的单一系统可以推广到具有高精度远程操作的人形手、手臂手、手臂夹持器和四足夹持器系统。这使得在不同平台上进行复杂操作任务的模仿学习成为可能。
Learning from demonstrations has proven to be an effective method for robotic manipulation, especially with the recent collection of large-scale robotic data with teleoperation systems. Building an efficient teleoperation system across different robotic platforms has become more important than ever. However, there is a clear lack of cost-effective and user-friendly teleoperation systems for different end effectors (e.g., anthropomorphic robot hands and grippers) that can run across multiple platforms.
To address this problem, scholars from the University of California, San Diego developed ACE, a cross-platform visual exoskeleton system for low-cost dexterous teleoperation. The scholars' system uses a hand-facing camera to capture 3D hand poses and uses an exoskeleton mounted on a portable base to accurately capture finger and wrist poses in real time. Compared to previous systems, which often require hardware customization for different robots, their single system can be generalized to humanoid hands, arm hands, arm grippers, and quadruped gripper systems with high-precision teleoperation. This makes imitation learning for complex manipulation tasks on different platforms possible
13.BiGym: A Demo-Driven Mobile Bi-Manual Manipulation Benchmark
BiGym:演示驱动的移动双手操作基准
在本文中，来自Dyson 机器人学习实验室的学者们推出了 BiGym，这是一个用于移动双手演示驱动机器人操作的全新基准和学习环境。BiGym 具有 40 个不同的家庭环境任务，从简单的目标到达到复杂的厨房清洁。为了准确捕捉现实世界的表现，学者们为每项任务提供了人工收集的演示，反映了现实世界机器人轨迹中的各种模式。BiGym 支持各种观察，包括本体感受数据和视觉输入（例如 RGB）以及来自 3 个摄像头视图的深度。为了验证 BiGym 的可用性，学者们在环境中对最先进的模仿学习算法和演示驱动的强化学习算法进行了全面的基准测试，并讨论了未来的机会。
In this paper, researchers from the Dyson Robot Learning Lab introduce BiGym, a new benchmark and learning environment for mobile two-handed demonstration-driven robotic manipulation. BiGym features 40 different home environment tasks, ranging from simple goal reaching to complex kitchen cleaning. To accurately capture real-world performance, researchers provide manually collected demonstrations for each task, reflecting various patterns in real-world robot trajectories. BiGym supports a variety of observations, including proprioceptive data and visual inputs (e.g., RGB) and depth from 3 camera views. To validate the usability of BiGym, researchers conduct a comprehensive benchmark of state-of-the-art imitation learning algorithms and demonstration-driven reinforcement learning algorithms in the environment, and discuss future opportunities.
14.Learning Smooth Humanoid Locomotion through Lipschitz-Constrained Policies
通过 Lipschitz 约束策略学习平滑的人形运动
强化学习与模拟到现实的迁移相结合，为开发腿式机器人的运动控制器提供了一个通用框架。为了便于在现实世界中成功部署，学者们通常会采用平滑技术（例如低通滤波器和平滑度奖励）来开发具有平滑行为的策略。但是，由于这些技术是不可微分的，并且通常需要对大量超参数进行繁琐的调整，因此它们往往需要对每个机器人平台进行大量的手动调整。
为了应对这一挑战并建立一种强制执行平滑行为的通用技术，来自西蒙弗雷泽大学和加州大学伯克利分校以及斯坦福大学的学者们提出了一种简单有效的方法，对学习到的策略施加 Lipschitz 约束，学者们将其称为 Lipschitz 约束策略 (LCP)。他们表明 Lipschitz 约束可以以梯度惩罚的形式实现，这提供了一个可微分的目标，可以轻松地与自动微分框架相结合。学者们证明了 LCP 有效地取代了对平滑奖励或低通滤波器的需求，并且可以轻松集成到许多不同人形机器人的训练框架中，并且对模拟和现实世界的人形机器人中的 LCP 进行了广泛评估，制作了流畅而强大的运动控制器。
Reinforcement learning combined with simulation-to-reality transfer provides a general framework for developing motion controllers for legged robots. To facilitate successful deployment in the real world, researchers often employ smoothing techniques such as low-pass filters and smoothness rewards to develop policies with smooth behavior. However, since these techniques are non-differentiable and often require tedious tuning of a large number of hyperparameters, they often require extensive manual tuning for each robotic platform.
To address this challenge and establish a general technique for enforcing smooth behavior, researchers from Simon Fraser University and the University of California, Berkeley, and Stanford University proposed a simple and effective method to impose Lipschitz constraints on the learned policy, which the researchers call Lipschitz Constrained Policy (LCP). They show that the Lipschitz constraint can be implemented in the form of a gradient penalty, which provides a differentiable objective that can be easily combined with the automatic differentiation framework. The scholars demonstrated that LCP effectively replaces the need for smooth rewards or low-pass filters and can be easily integrated into the training frameworks of many different humanoid robots. They also extensively evaluated LCP in simulated and real-world humanoid robots, producing a smooth and powerful motion controller.
15.Learning Getting-Up Policies for Real-World Humanoid Robots
学习现实世界人形机器人的起身策略
跌倒后自动起身恢复是人形机器人可靠部署的关键先决条件。由于人形机器人跌倒后可能处于各种不同的姿势，并且人形机器人需要在具有挑战性的地形上运行，因此手动设计起身控制器非常困难。
在本文中，来自伊利诺伊大学和西蒙弗雷泽大学的学者们开发了一个学习框架来生成控制器，使人形机器人能够从不同地形的不同姿势下起身。与之前成功的人形运动学习应用不同，起身任务涉及复杂的接触模式，这需要准确建模碰撞几何和更稀疏的奖励。学者们通过遵循课程的两阶段方法来解决这些挑战。第一阶段侧重于在平滑度或速度/扭矩限制的最小约束下发现良好的起身轨迹。然后，第二阶段将发现的动作细化为可部署的（即平滑和缓慢的）动作，这些动作对初始配置和地形的变化具有鲁棒性。学者们发现这些创新使现实世界中的 G1 人形机器人能够从他们考虑的两种主要情况中站起来：a) 仰卧和 b) 俯卧，这两种情况都是在平坦、可变形、光滑的表面和斜坡上进行的测试（例如，湿滑的草地和雪地）。据学者们所知，这是现实世界中首次成功演示人类大小的人形机器人学习到的站起策略。
Automatic recovery after a fall is a key prerequisite for reliable deployment of humanoid robots. Manually designing a get-up controller is difficult because humanoid robots may be in a variety of different postures after a fall and humanoid robots need to operate on challenging terrains.
In this paper, scholars from the University of Illinois and Simon Fraser University developed a learning framework to generate controllers that enable humanoid robots to get up from different postures on different terrains. Unlike previous successful humanoid motion learning applications, the get-up task involves complex contact patterns, which requires accurate modeling of collision geometry and sparser rewards. Scholars address these challenges by following a two-stage approach that follows a curriculum. The first stage focuses on discovering good get-up trajectories under minimal constraints of smoothness or speed/torque limits. Then, the second stage refines the discovered actions into deployable (i.e., smooth and slow) actions that are robust to changes in the initial configuration and terrain. The researchers found that these innovations enabled a real-world G1 humanoid robot to stand up from the two main situations they considered: a) lying on its back and b) lying on its stomach, both of which were tested on flat, deformable, smooth surfaces and slopes (e.g., slippery grass and snow). To the researchers’ knowledge, this is the first successful demonstration of a learned standing-up strategy for a human-sized humanoid robot in the real world.
16.Learning Humanoid Standing-up Control across Diverse Postures
学习在不同姿势下控制人形站立
站立控制对于人形机器人至关重要，有可能集成到当前的运动和操纵系统中，例如跌倒恢复。现有的方法要么仅限于忽略硬件限制的模拟，要么依赖于预定义的地面特定运动轨迹，无法在现实场景中实现跨姿势站立。
为了弥补这一差距，来自上海交通大学,上海人工智能实验室, 香港大学,浙江大学和香港中文大学的学者们提出了 HoST（人形站立控制），这是一个强化学习框架，可以从头开始学习站立控制，实现跨不同姿势的稳健模拟到现实转移。HoST 通过利用多评论家架构和基于课程的训练在不同的模拟地形上有效地学习姿势自适应运动。为了确保成功部署到现实世界，学者们分别使用平滑度正则化和隐式运动速度约束来限制运动，以减轻物理硬件上的振荡和剧烈运动。经过基于模拟的训练后，学习到的控制策略直接部署在 Unitree G1 人形机器人上。学者们的实验结果表明，控制器在各种实验室和户外环境中实现平稳、稳定、稳健的站立运动。
Standing control is crucial for humanoid robots and has the potential to be integrated into current motion and manipulation systems, such as fall recovery. Existing methods are either limited to simulations that ignore hardware limitations or rely on predefined ground-specific motion trajectories, which cannot achieve cross-pose standing in real-world scenarios.
To bridge this gap, scholars from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, University of Hong Kong, Zhejiang University, and Chinese University of Hong Kong proposed HoST (Humanoid Standing Control), a reinforcement learning framework that learns standing control from scratch and achieves robust simulation-to-reality transfer across different poses. HoST effectively learns posture-adaptive motion on different simulated terrains by leveraging a multi-critic architecture and curriculum-based training. To ensure successful deployment in the real world, scholars constrain motion using smoothness regularization and implicit motion velocity constraints, respectively, to mitigate oscillations and violent motions on physical hardware. After simulation-based training, the learned control policy is directly deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. The scholars' experimental results show that the controller achieves smooth, stable, and robust standing motion in a variety of laboratory and outdoor environments.
17.SPARK: A Modular Benchmark for Humanoid Robot Safety
SPARK：人形机器人安全性的模块化基准
在本文中，来自卡内基梅隆大学机器人研究所的学者们介绍了安全防护和辅助机器人套件 (SPARK)，这是一个全面的基准，旨在确保人形机器人自主和远程操作的安全。人形机器人具有与复杂环境交互的物理能力，因此存在重大的安全风险。人形机器人的物理结构进一步增加了通用安全解决方案设计的复杂性。为了促进复杂机器人系统的安全部署，SPARK 可用作一个工具箱，该工具箱配备了模块化和可组合的机器人控制框架中最先进的安全控制算法。用户可以轻松配置安全标准和灵敏度级别，以优化安全性和性能之间的平衡。为了加速人形机器人安全研究和开发，SPARK 提供了一个模拟基准，可以比较各种环境、任务和机器人模型中的安全方法。此外，SPARK 允许在真实机器人上快速部署合成的安全控制器。对于硬件部署，SPARK 支持 Apple Vision Pro (AVP) 或运动捕捉系统作为外部传感器，同时还提供与替代硬件设置无缝集成的接口。本文通过 Unitree G1 人形机器人的仿真实验和案例研究展示了 SPARK 的能力。利用 SPARK 的这些优势，用户和研究人员可以显著提高其人形系统的安全性并加速相关研究。
In this paper, scholars from the Robotics Institute at Carnegie Mellon University present the Safe Guarding and Assistive Robotics Kit (SPARK), a comprehensive benchmark designed to ensure the safety of autonomous and teleoperation of humanoid robots. Humanoid robots present significant safety risks due to their physical ability to interact with complex environments. The physical structure of humanoid robots further increases the complexity of designing general safety solutions. To facilitate the safe deployment of complex robotic systems, SPARK serves as a toolbox equipped with state-of-the-art safety control algorithms in a modular and composable robotic control framework. Users can easily configure safety criteria and sensitivity levels to optimize the balance between safety and performance. To accelerate humanoid robot safety research and development, SPARK provides a simulation benchmark that allows comparison of safety methods in a variety of environments, tasks, and robot models. In addition, SPARK allows for rapid deployment of synthetic safety controllers on real robots. For hardware deployment, SPARK supports Apple Vision Pro (AVP) or motion capture systems as external sensors, while also providing interfaces for seamless integration with alternative hardware setups. This paper demonstrates the capabilities of SPARK through simulation experiments and case studies on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. By leveraging these advantages of SPARK, users and researchers can significantly improve the safety of their humanoid systems and accelerate related research.
18.Dexterous Safe Control for Humanoids in Cluttered Environments via Projected Safe Set Algorithm
通过投影安全集算法实现杂乱环境中人形机器人的灵巧安全控制
在不影响性能的情况下，确保人形机器人在实际应用中的安全性至关重要。在本文中，来自卡内基梅隆大学机器人研究所的学者们考虑了灵巧安全性问题，其特点是肢体级几何约束，以避免杂乱环境中的外部和自碰撞。与在 sprase 环境中具有简化边界几何的安全性相比，灵巧安全性会产生许多约束，这些约束在解决安全机器人控制问题时通常会导致不可行的约束集。为了解决这个问题，学者们提出了投影安全集算法 (p-SSA)，这是经典安全控制算法向多约束情况的扩展。p-SSA 以原则性的方式放宽了相互冲突的约束，最大限度地减少了安全违规行为，从而保证了可行的机器人控制。学者们在模拟和执行复杂防撞任务的真实 Unitree G1 人形机器人上验证了他们的方法。结果表明，p-SSA 使人形机器人能够在具有挑战性的情况下以最少的安全违规行为稳健地运行，并且无需参数调整即可直接推广到各种任务。
Ensuring the safety of humanoid robots in real-world applications without compromising performance is of vital importance. In this paper, scholars from the Robotics Institute of Carnegie Mellon University consider the problem of dexterous safety, which is characterized by limb-level geometric constraints to avoid external and self-collisions in cluttered environments. Compared with safety with simplified boundary geometry in sprase environments, dexterous safety generates many constraints that often lead to infeasible constraint sets when solving the problem of safe robot control. To address this issue, scholars propose the projected safe set algorithm (p-SSA), an extension of the classical safe control algorithm to the multi-constraint case. p-SSA relaxes the conflicting constraints in a principled way, minimizing safety violations and thus ensuring feasible robot control. Scholars validate their approach on a real Unitree G1 humanoid robot in simulation and performing complex collision avoidance tasks. Results show that p-SSA enables humanoid robots to operate robustly in challenging situations with minimal safety violations and can be directly generalized to a variety of tasks without parameter tuning.
19.ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills
ASAP：结合模拟和真实世界物理，学习敏捷人形机器人全身技能
人形机器人在执行类似人类的全身技能方面具有无与伦比的多功能性。然而，由于模拟和现实世界之间的动态不匹配，实现敏捷和协调的全身运动仍然是一项重大挑战。现有方法，例如系统识别 (SysID) 和域随机化 (DR) 方法，通常依赖于劳动密集型参数调整，或导致过于保守的策略而牺牲敏捷性。
在本文中，来自卡内基梅隆大学和NVIDIA的学者们提出了 ASAP（对齐模拟和现实世界物理），这是一个两阶段框架，旨在解决动态不匹配问题并实现敏捷的人形全身技能。在第一阶段，学者们使用重新定位的人体运动数据在模拟中预训练运动跟踪策略。在第二阶段，学者们在现实世界中部署策略并收集现实世界数据以训练增量（残差）动作模型来补偿动态不匹配。然后，ASAP 使用集成到模拟器中的增量动作模型对预训练策略进行微调，以有效地与现实世界动态保持一致。学者们在三种转移场景中评估了 ASAP：从 IsaacGym 到 IsaacSim、从 IsaacGym 到 Genesis，以及从 IsaacGym 到现实世界的 Unitree G1 人形机器人。他们的方法显著提高了各种动态运动中的敏捷性和全身协调性，与 SysID、DR 和 delta 动力学学习基线相比，减少了跟踪误差。ASAP 实现了以前难以实现的高度敏捷运动，展示了 delta 动作学习在连接模拟和现实世界动态方面的潜力。这些结果表明，从模拟到现实，开发更具表现力和敏捷性的人形机器人是一个有希望的方向。
Humanoid robots have unparalleled versatility in performing human-like full-body skills. However, achieving agile and coordinated full-body motion remains a major challenge due to the dynamic mismatch between simulation and the real world. Existing methods, such as system identification (SysID) and domain randomization (DR) methods, often rely on labor-intensive parameter tuning or lead to overly conservative policies that sacrifice agility.
In this paper, scholars from Carnegie Mellon University and NVIDIA propose ASAP (Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics), a two-stage framework designed to address the dynamic mismatch problem and achieve agile humanoid full-body skills. In the first stage, scholars pre-train a motion tracking policy in simulation using re-targeted human motion data. In the second stage, scholars deploy the policy in the real world and collect real-world data to train an incremental (residual) action model to compensate for the dynamic mismatch. Then, ASAP fine-tunes the pre-trained policy using the incremental action model integrated into the simulator to effectively align with the real-world dynamics. The scholars evaluated ASAP in three transfer scenarios: from IsaacGym to IsaacSim, from IsaacGym to Genesis, and from IsaacGym to the real-world Unitree G1 humanoid robot. Their method significantly improved agility and whole-body coordination in a variety of dynamic movements, reducing tracking errors compared to SysID, DR, and delta dynamics learning baselines. ASAP achieved highly agile movements that were previously difficult to achieve, demonstrating the potential of delta motion learning in connecting simulation and real-world dynamics. These results suggest that developing more expressive and agile humanoid robots from simulation to reality is a promising direction.
20.Continual Learning and Lifting of Koopman Dynamics for Linear Control of Legged Robots
持续学习和提升库普曼动力学以实现腿式机器人的线性控制
由于高维和非线性动力学，腿式机器人（尤其是人形机器人和四足机器人）的控制面临巨大挑战。虽然可以使用模型预测控制 (MPC) 等方法有效控制线性系统，但非线性系统的控制仍然很复杂。一种有前途的解决方案是 Koopman 算子，它使用线性模型近似非线性动力学，从而可以使用成熟的线性控制技术。然而，由于近似误差、域偏移和固定线性状态空间表示的局限性等问题，通过数据驱动方法实现精确线性化很困难。这些挑战限制了基于 Koopman 的方法的可扩展性。
本文中，来自卡内基梅隆大学机器人研究所的学者们通过提出一种持续学习算法来解决这些挑战，该算法旨在迭代改进高维腿式机器人的 Koopman 动力学。关键思想是逐步扩展数据集和潜在空间维度，使学习到的 Koopman 动力学能够收敛到真实系统动力学的精确近似值。理论分析表明，学者们的方法的线性近似误差单调收敛。实验结果表明，学者们的方法使用简单的线性 MPC 控制器在各种地形上对 Unitree G1/H1/A1/Go2 和 ANYmal D 等机器人实现了高控制性能。这项工作首次成功将线性化 Koopman 动力学应用于高维腿式机器人的运动控制，从而实现了可扩展的基于模型的控制解决方案。
The control of legged robots, especially humanoids and quadrupeds, faces great challenges due to their high-dimensional and nonlinear dynamics. While linear systems can be effectively controlled using methods such as model predictive control (MPC), the control of nonlinear systems remains complex. A promising solution is the Koopman operator, which approximates nonlinear dynamics using a linear model, allowing the use of well-established linear control techniques. However, accurate linearization via data-driven methods is difficult due to issues such as approximation errors, domain shift, and limitations of fixed linear state space representations. These challenges limit the scalability of Koopman-based methods.
In this paper, scholars from the Robotics Institute at Carnegie Mellon University address these challenges by proposing a continual learning algorithm that aims to iteratively improve the Koopman dynamics of high-dimensional legged robots. The key idea is to gradually expand the dataset and the latent space dimensionality so that the learned Koopman dynamics can converge to an accurate approximation of the true system dynamics. Theoretical analysis shows that the linear approximation error of the scholars' method converges monotonically. Experimental results show that our approach achieves high control performance on various terrains for robots such as Unitree G1/H1/A1/Go2 and ANYmal D using a simple linear MPC controller. This work successfully applies linearized Koopman dynamics to the motion control of high-dimensional legged robots for the first time, thus achieving a scalable model-based control solution.
21. GRUtopia: Dream General Robots in a City at Scale
格鲁托皮亚：城市规模中的梦幻通用机器人。
来自OpenRobotLab与上海AI实验室的研究团队指出，当前具身智能（Embodied AI）领域面临真实数据采集成本高昂的挑战，而仿真到现实（Sim2Real）范式是规模化训练具身模型的关键。为此，团队推出首个面向多类机器人的交互式3D仿真社会项目“GRUtopia”，其创新包括：(a) 场景数据集GRScenes涵盖10万个可自由组合的精细标注交互场景，覆盖89类服务导向环境，弥补了现有研究集中于家庭场景的不足；(b) 基于大语言模型（LLM）的虚拟居民系统GRResidents，能模拟社交互动、任务生成与分配；(c) 基准测试GRBench以足式机器人为核心，支持物体移动导航、社交导航及移动操作等中等难度任务。该项目旨在缓解高质量数据稀缺问题，推动具身AI研究的全面评估。
A research team from OpenRobotLab and Shanghai AI Laboratory highlighted the challenge of prohibitive real-world data collection costs in Embodied AI, emphasizing that the Simulation-to-Real (Sim2Real) paradigm is pivotal for scaling embodied model training. They introduced "GRUtopia," the first interactive 3D simulated society for diverse robots, featuring: (a) GRScenes, a dataset of 100k finely annotated, combinable scenes spanning 89 service-oriented categories, addressing the gap in home-centric prior works; (b) GRResidents, an LLM-driven NPC system simulating social interactions, task generation, and assignment; (c) GRBench, a benchmark focusing on legged robots with moderately challenging tasks like Object Loco-Navigation and Loco-Manipulation. The project aims to alleviate data scarcity and advance comprehensive Embodied AI evaluation.
22. Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates
for Dexterous Medical Interventions
医院中的人形机器人：灵巧医疗干预用人形替代体的技术研究
加州大学圣地亚哥分校（UC San Diego）的研究团队针对人口老龄化和医护人员短缺导致的医疗压力问题，探索了人形机器人通过遥操作执行临床任务的可行性。团队为Unitree G1人形机器人开发了一套双臂遥操作系统，整合了高精度姿态追踪、定制化抓取配置和阻抗控制器，以安全精准地操作医疗工具。该系统在七类医疗场景（包括体格检查、急救干预和精密针头操作）中表现突出，尤其在人工通气和超声引导任务中展现出量化性能优势。然而，研究也揭示了人形机器人在高强度输出和临床精度传感器灵敏度方面的局限性。这项研究为未来机器人医疗集成提供了技术基础，同时指明了需突破的关键瓶颈。
Researchers from UC San Diego addressed healthcare pressures caused by aging populations and labor shortages by exploring the feasibility of humanoid robots performing clinical tasks via teleoperation. They developed a bimanual teleoperation system for the Unitree G1 Humanoid Robot, integrating high-fidelity pose tracking, custom grasping configurations, and an impedance controller to manipulate medical tools safely and precisely. The system excelled in seven medical scenarios—including physical examinations, emergency interventions, and precision needle tasks—demonstrating quantitative performance advantages in ventilation and ultrasound-guided procedures. However, limitations in force output for high-strength tasks and sensor sensitivity affecting clinical accuracy were identified. This study lays technical groundwork for robotic healthcare integration while pinpointing critical challenges for future breakthroughs.
23. HOMIE: Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Isomorphic Exoskeleton Cockpit
HOMIE：基于同构外骨骼驾驶舱的人形机器人移动操控系统
香港中文大学多媒体实验室的研究团队针对人形机器人全身协调控制与高精度物体操作的难题，开发了半自主遥操作系统HOMIE。该系统创新性地融合了踏板映射强化学习策略（用于身体控制）、同构外骨骼机械臂（用于手臂控制）和运动传感手套（用于手部控制），形成统一操作舱，可自由操控人形机器人并建立数据闭环。其强化学习策略采用上身姿态课程学习、高度追踪奖励等新设计，使机器人能完成行走、蹲姿调整等任务；外骨骼摒弃逆动力学依赖，实现更快更精准的手臂控制；手套采用霍尔传感器替代伺服电机，在紧凑结构中支持15+自由度并适配各类灵巧手模型。相比现有系统，HOMIE以500美元的低成本实现任务效率翻倍、工作范围扩展（可自由触及高低空间及任意物体交互），为通用化人形机器人操作树立了新标杆。
Researchers from CUHK's Multimedia Laboratory tackled the challenge of generalizable humanoid loco-manipulation by developing HOMIE, a semi-autonomous teleoperation system. It integrates a pedal-mapped RL policy for body control, an isomorphic exoskeleton arm for precise arm manipulation, and motion-sensing gloves for dexterous hand control, forming a unified cockpit that establishes a data flywheel. The RL policy incorporates novel designs like upper-body pose curriculum learning and height-tracking rewards, enabling adaptive walking/squatting. The exoskeleton achieves faster arm control by bypassing inverse dynamics, while Hall sensor-based gloves support 15+ DoF in compact designs. Priced at $500, HOMIE doubles task efficiency, expands workspace accessibility (reaching high/low areas and arbitrary objects), and sets a new benchmark for affordable humanoid teleoperation.
24. ExBody2: Advanced Expressive Humanoid Whole-Body Control
ExBody2：高级拟人化全身运动控制系统
来自加州大学圣地亚哥分校、麻省理工学院和加州大学伯克利分校的联合研究团队开发了"高级全身表情控制系统（Exbody2）"，成功解决了人形机器人在保持整体稳定性的同时实现动态全身动作的难题。该系统创新性地采用两步训练法：首先通过教师策略生成符合机器人运动学的中介数据并过滤不可行动作，随后训练学生策略实现真实世界的行走、蹲伏和舞蹈等复杂动作。研究还揭示了动作泛化能力与特定动作追踪精度之间的平衡关系——少量数据微调即可显著提升特定动作表现，但会牺牲其他动作的适应性。该技术为人形机器人自然运动控制提供了新范式。
A joint research team from UC San Diego, MIT and UC Berkeley has developed "Advanced Expressive Whole-Body Control (Exbody2)" that enables humanoid robots to perform dynamic full-body motions while maintaining stability. The system innovatively employs a two-stage training approach: first generating kinematically feasible intermediary data through teacher policy filtering, then training student policy for real-world deployment of complex motions like walking, crouching and dancing. The study also reveals the trade-off between motion generalization and specific action tracking accuracy - fine-tuning with minimal data significantly improves targeted motion performance at the cost of adaptability. This breakthrough establishes a new paradigm for natural movement control in humanoid robots.
25. COMPASS: Cross-embOdiment Mobility Policy via ResiduAl RL and Skill Synthesis
COMPASS：基于残差强化学习与技能合成的跨形态移动策略系统
英伟达、加州大学伯克利分校和德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的研究团队联合开发了"COMPASS：基于残差强化学习与技能合成的跨形态移动策略系统"。面对机器人多样化部署带来的跨平台移动控制难题，该研究创新性地结合模仿学习(IL)、残差强化学习(RL)和策略蒸馏技术，提出三阶段解决方案：首先通过模仿学习构建融合世界模型的基础移动策略；继而采用残差强化学习针对不同机器人形态进行高效调优；最后通过策略蒸馏整合为统一策略。实验表明，该框架在多样化机器人平台上实现约5倍于基础IL策略的成功率，为异构机器人群体在复杂场景中的自主导航提供了高效可扩展的新范式。
A research collaboration between Nvidia, UC Berkeley and UT Austin has developed "COMPASS: Cross-embOdiment Mobility Policy via ResiduAl RL and Skill Synthesis". Addressing the challenge of cross-platform mobility control for diverse robots, this work innovatively integrates imitation learning (IL), residual reinforcement learning (RL) and policy distillation in a three-phase approach: first constructing foundational mobility policies with world models via IL, then efficiently fine-tuning for different embodiments through residual RL, and finally consolidating into a unified policy via distillation. Experiments demonstrate the framework achieves approximately 5X higher success rates than baseline IL policies across diverse robot platforms, establishing an efficient and scalable new paradigm for autonomous navigation of heterogeneous robot teams in complex scenarios.
26. HumanoidOlympics: Sports Environments for Physically Simulated Humanoids
HumanoidOlympics：面向物理仿真人形机器的体育竞技环境
一项名为"HumanoidOlympics"的创新研究为动画与机器人领域带来了突破性进展——该研究构建了包含高尔夫、标枪、跳高、跨栏等个人项目及乒乓球、击剑、足球等竞技项目的虚拟奥运赛场。这套物理仿真系统同时支持图形化角色(SMPL/SMPL-X模型)与实际机器人的运动测试，通过专家设计的奖励机制产生了令人惊艳的仿真效果。研究表明，融入人类动作示范能显著提升策略的拟人化程度与任务表现。作为首个标准化的体育竞技测试平台，HumanoidOlympics为开发拟人化高性能控制器提供了全新研究范式。
The groundbreaking "HumanoidOlympics" research introduces a virtual Olympic arena featuring individual sports (golf, javelin, high jump, etc.) and competitive games (table tennis, fencing, soccer, etc.) for animation and robotics development. This physics-based simulation system supports both graphical characters (SMPL/SMPL-X models) and real-world robots, generating impressive results through expert-designed reward mechanisms. The study demonstrates that incorporating human demonstrations significantly enhances policy human-likeness and task performance. As the first standardized sports benchmark, HumanoidOlympics establishes a new paradigm for developing human-like high-performance controllers.
27. Post-Convergence Sim-to-Real Policy Transfer: A Principled Alternative to Cherry-Picking
收敛后仿真到现实策略迁移：一种基于原则的经验筛选替代方案
爱荷华州立大学计算机科学团队针对强化学习策略从仿真到现实迁移中的"经验筛选"难题，创新性地提出了"收敛后迁移优化框架"。传统方法多在收敛前阶段采用域随机化等技术改进迁移效果，但无法避免策略性能波动导致的启发性筛选问题。该研究将迁移过程建模为凸二次约束线性规划问题，通过最坏情况性能优化确保策略鲁棒性。在足式机器人运动控制任务中，该方法显著提升了仿真策略在真实实验室环境中的稳定表现，为自主智能体的可靠部署提供了理论保障。
Researchers from Iowa State University's Computer Science Department have developed a novel "post-convergence transfer optimization framework" addressing the cherry-picking dilemma in sim-to-real policy transfer. While conventional approaches focus on pre-convergence improvements like domain randomization, they cannot eliminate performance fluctuations that necessitate heuristic selection. By formulating the transfer process as a convex quadratically-constrained linear program, the method ensures robustness through worst-case performance optimization. Extensive experiments on legged robot locomotion demonstrate significantly enhanced real-world policy stability, providing theoretical guarantees for reliable autonomous agent deployment.
28. I-CTRL Imitation to Control Humanoid Robots Through Bounded Residual Reinforcement Learning
I-CTRL：通过有界残差强化学习实现仿人机器人控制的模仿学习框架
维也纳工业大学与德国宇航中心联合团队开发了"I-CTRL"仿人机器人控制框架，通过有界残差强化学习技术实现了人类动作的高保真物理重现。该研究突破性地将动作模仿转化为对非物理重定向动作的约束优化，仅需简单统一的奖励函数即可在五种不同机器人上实现泛化控制。框架创新的自动优先级调度器有效管理大规模动作数据集训练，解决了双足机器人视觉保真与物理可行性难以兼顾的行业难题，为仿人机器人实用化部署树立了新标准。
A joint research team from TU Wien and DLR has developed the "I-CTRL" framework for humanoid robot control, achieving high-fidelity physical reproduction of human motions through bounded residual reinforcement learning. The study reformulates motion imitation as constrained optimization of non-physics-based retargeting, requiring only simple unified rewards to enable generalized control across five robot platforms. The framework's innovative automatic priority scheduler efficiently handles large-scale motion dataset training, solving the industry challenge of balancing visual fidelity with physical feasibility for bipedal robots, setting new standards for practical humanoid deployment.
29. UMC: Unified Resilient Controller for Legged Robots with Joint Malfunctions
UMC：面向关节故障足式机器人的统一弹性控制器
四川大学、上海AI实验室等机构联合研发的"UMC统一故障控制器"为足式机器人带来突破性容错能力。该研究首次系统归纳八类机器人损伤场景，创新性提出两阶段训练框架：首阶段确保标准环境下的稳健性能，次阶段通过掩码机制使机器人自主规避故障肢体依赖。实验显示，该方案在三种运动任务中平均提升Transformer模型36%、MLP模型39%的任务完成率，为足式机器人在传感器失效、关节故障等意外损伤下的自主适应提供了通用解决方案。
The "UMC Unified Malfunction Controller" developed by Sichuan University, Shanghai AI Lab and collaborators delivers breakthrough fault-tolerance for legged robots. This work systematically categorizes eight damage scenarios for the first time, introducing a novel two-stage framework: initial training ensures robust baseline performance, while masked training enables autonomous adaptation to malfunctioning limbs. Experiments show 36% (Transformer) and 39% (MLP) average improvement in task completion across three locomotion scenarios, providing a universal solution for autonomous adaptation to sensor/joint failures.
30. VR-Robo: A Real-to-Sim-to-Real Framework for Visual Robot Navigation and Locomotion
VR-Robo：面向机器人视觉导航与运动的虚实融合框架
清华大学、上海期智研究院等机构联合提出"VR-Robo"虚实融合框架，通过3D高斯泼溅技术构建具备物理交互能力的数字孪生环境，首次实现纯RGB视觉导航策略的仿真到现实迁移。该框架利用多视角图像重建高真实感场景，支持以第一人称视角进行强化学习训练，在家庭和工厂等复杂新环境中展现出卓越的探索适应能力，为机器人视觉导航与运动控制提供了端到端的解决方案。
A collaborative team from Tsinghua University and Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute developed "VR-Robo", a real-to-sim-to-real framework that employs 3D Gaussian Splatting to create physics-enabled digital twin environments, achieving the first RGB-only sim-to-real transfer for visual navigation policies. By reconstructing photorealistic scenes from multi-view images, this end-to-end solution supports egocentric reinforcement learning training and demonstrates superior exploration adaptability in novel household/factory environments.
31. Guiding Collision-Free Humanoid Multi-Contact Locomotion using Convex Kinematic Relaxations and Dynamic Optimization
基于凸运动学松弛与动态优化的仿人机器人无碰撞多接触运动引导框架
德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校航空航天工程团队创新性地提出"基于凸优化的仿人机器人多接触运动规划框架"，通过将无碰撞路径规划松弛为凸优化问题，并结合动态轨迹优化器，成功解决了传统方法在大型障碍物或运动极限场景下的规划失效难题。该框架能在数秒内生成包含多接触状态的动态可行运动方案，仿真实验中三种不同尺寸的仿人机器人均成功完成高门槛海军舱门的穿越任务，为复杂非结构化环境中的机器人导航提供了高效解决方案。
Researchers from UT Austin's Aerospace Engineering Department proposed an innovative convex-optimization-based framework for humanoid multi-contact locomotion planning. By reformulating collision-free path planning as convex optimization problems and integrating dynamic trajectory optimization, the method overcomes traditional planners' failures when handling large obstacles or kinematic limits. The framework generates dynamically feasible multi-contact motions within seconds, successfully enabling three humanoid robots of different sizes to traverse raised naval doors in simulation, providing an efficient solution for navigation in complex unstructured environments.
32. Toward Task Generalization via Memory Augmentation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning
通过记忆增强实现元强化学习的任务泛化
苏黎世联邦理工学院机械与过程工程系团队提出"基于记忆增强的元强化学习框架"，通过任务结构化增强模拟分布外场景，结合记忆机制实现上下文感知的策略适应。该框架在预定义任务集上训练后，无需额外环境交互即可通过记忆增强实现对新任务的零样本泛化。在足式机器人运动任务的仿真与实物实验中，该方法在保持分布内任务稳健性能的同时，展现出对未见任务的高效适应能力，为强化学习在动态多变场景中的广泛应用提供了新思路。
Researchers from ETH Zurich's Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering developed a memory-augmented meta-reinforcement learning framework that employs task-structured augmentations to simulate out-of-distribution scenarios and memory mechanisms for context-aware policy adaptation. Trained on predefined tasks, the policy achieves zero-shot generalization to novel tasks without additional environmental interactions. Extensive simulations and hardware experiments on legged locomotion demonstrate robust in-distribution performance while efficiently adapting to unseen tasks, advancing RL deployment in dynamic scenarios.
33. Physically Consistent Humanoid Loco-Manipulation using Latent Diffusion Models
基于潜在扩散模型的物理一致仿人机器人运动操作规划
慕尼黑工业大学与纽约大学团队创新性地将潜在扩散模型(LDMs)应用于仿人机器人运动规划，通过生成逼真的人-物交互场景RGB图像，从中提取接触点与机器人构型信息，进而指导全身轨迹优化生成物理一致的长时程运动方案。研究在多种长时程操作场景的仿真验证表明，该框架能有效协调视觉生成与物理约束，为需要复杂推理的仿人机器人操作任务提供了新范式。
A joint team from Technical University of Munich and NYU pioneered the application of Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs) to humanoid motion planning. By generating photorealistic human-object interaction images and extracting contact points/robot configurations, the framework guides whole-body trajectory optimization to produce physically consistent long-horizon motions. Simulation validations across diverse manipulation scenarios demonstrate its capability to harmonize visual generation with physical constraints, establishing a new paradigm for complex reasoning tasks in humanoid robotics.
34. InterMimic: Towards Universal Whole-Body Control for Physics-Based Human-Object Interactions
InterMimic：面向物理人-物交互的通用全身控制框架
伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校与电子艺界（EA）联合研发的"InterMimic"框架，通过潜在扩散模型生成逼真的人-物交互场景，并从中提取接触点与机器人构型信息，进而指导全身轨迹优化生成物理一致的运动方案。该研究在多种长时程操作场景的仿真验证中，证明了基于视觉生成信息的物理一致性轨迹规划能力，为通用化仿人机器人全身控制提供了新范式。
The "InterMimic" framework, jointly developed by University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Electronic Arts (EA), employs Latent Diffusion Models to generate photorealistic human-object interaction scenes, extracting contact points and robot configurations to guide whole-body trajectory optimization. Extensive simulation validations across long-horizon manipulation scenarios demonstrate its capability to produce physically consistent motions from visual generation, establishing a new paradigm for universal whole-body humanoid control.
35. Humanoid-VLA: Towards Universal Humanoid Control with Visual Integration
Humanoid-VLA：基于视觉语言融合的通用仿人机器人控制框架
西湖大学、浙江大学等机构联合研发的"Humanoid-VLA"框架，通过语言-运动预对齐、视觉条件微调与自监督数据增强三大创新技术，首次实现语言理解、第一人称场景感知与运动控制的深度融合。该框架利用非第一人称人类运动数据集与文本描述进行预训练，再通过参数高效的视觉条件微调实现环境感知，配合自动生成的运动数据伪标注策略，使仿人机器人展现出类人的环境交互与自适应探索能力，为通用化智能仿人控制树立了新标杆。
The "Humanoid-VLA" framework developed by Westlake University, Zhejiang University and collaborators pioneers the deep integration of language understanding, egocentric perception and motion control through three innovations: language-motion pre-alignment, parameter-efficient video-conditioned fine-tuning, and self-supervised data augmentation. By leveraging non-egocentric human motion datasets with textual descriptions and automatically generated pseudo-annotations, it enables humanoid robots to demonstrate human-like adaptive interaction and environmental exploration capabilities, setting new standards for universal intelligent humanoid control.
36. Variations of Augmented Lagrangian for Robotic Multi-Contact Simulation
面向机器人多接触仿真的增广拉格朗日变体算法研究
韩国首尔国立大学机械工程系团队在机器人多接触仿真领域取得突破性进展，提出基于增广拉格朗日理论的新型非线性互补问题求解框架。该研究创新性地开发了两种优化算法：级联牛顿增广拉格朗日法(CANAL)在保证高精度求解的同时提升鲁棒性，子系统交替方向乘子法(SubADMM)则针对高自由度多体系统实现超线性加速与并行计算。实验证明，该框架在密集接触与刚性交互场景中兼具计算效率与数值稳定性，为复杂机器人操作任务提供了可靠的仿真工具。
Researchers from Seoul National University's Mechanical Engineering Department made a breakthrough in robotic multi-contact simulation by proposing a novel nonlinear complementarity problem solver based on Augmented Lagrangian theory. The study innovatively developed two algorithms: the Cascaded Newton-based Augmented Lagrangian (CANAL) ensures high-precision solutions with enhanced robustness, while the Subsystem-based ADMM (SubADMM) achieves superlinear acceleration and parallel computing for high-DoF multibody systems. Experiments demonstrate the framework's computational efficiency and numerical stability in intensive contact scenarios, providing reliable simulation tools for complex robotic manipulation tasks.
37. Embrace Collisions: Humanoid Shadowing for Deployable Contact-Agnostics Motions
拥抱碰撞：面向可部署接触无关运动的仿人影子控制
清华大学智能产业研究院与上海期智研究院联合提出"接触无关仿人运动控制框架"，突破性地将机器人视为全身接触系统而非仅手脚交互平台。该研究利用GPU加速刚体仿真器训练全身控制策略，通过离散运动指令实时驱动机器人完成坐椅起身、地面翻滚等复杂动作，在存在随机接触、大幅基座旋转及非理想指令条件下仍保持稳定，为仿人机器人的实用化部署提供了新思路。
A joint team from Tsinghua IIIS and Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute proposed a contact-agnostic humanoid motion framework that redefines robots as full-body contact systems rather than just hand-foot interaction platforms. Leveraging GPU-accelerated rigid-body simulators, the trained whole-body control policy enables real-time execution of complex motions like chair-rising and floor-rolling under stochastic contacts, extreme base rotations, and suboptimal commands, advancing practical humanoid deployment.
38. Towards Dynamical Safety on Humanoids with Stochastic Controllers with SHIELD
面向类人机器人动态安全性的随机控制器护盾方法
机器人学习已为类人机器人动态运动等复杂任务生成了效率显著的“黑箱”控制器。然而，确保动态安全性（即约束满足）对于此类策略而言仍颇具挑战。强化学习（RL）通过奖励工程以启发式方式嵌入约束，且添加或修改约束需重新训练。基于模型的方法（如控制障碍函数，CBFs）支持带形式化保证的运行时约束规范，但依赖精确的动力学模型。本文提出 SHIELD—— 一种分层安全框架，通过以下方式弥合这一差距：（1）利用标称控制器硬件部署的真实数据训练生成式随机动力学残差模型，以捕捉系统行为与不确定性；（2）在标称（学习所得的运动）控制器之上叠加安全层，该层通过随机离散时间 CBF 公式利用所学残差模型，从概率层面强制实施轨迹全程的安全约束。最终形成的微创安全层可集成至现有自主系统栈，以优化用户指令跟踪并提供概率安全保证。在宇树 G1 类人机器人的硬件实验中，SHIELD 通过标称（未知）RL 控制器与机载感知，实现了在多样化室内外环境中的安全导航（避障）。
Robot learning has produced remarkably effective "black-box" controllers for complex tasks such as dynamic locomotion on humanoids. Yet ensuring dynamic safety, i.e., constraint satisfaction, remains challenging for such policies. Reinforcement learning (RL) embeds constraints heuristically through reward engineering, and adding or modifying constraints requires retraining. Model-based approaches, like control barrier functions (CBFs), enable runtime constraint specification with formal guarantees but require accurate dynamics models. This paper presents SHIELD, a layered safety framework that bridges this gap by: (1) training a generative, stochastic dynamics residual model using real-world data from hardware rollouts of the nominal controller, capturing system behavior and uncertainties; and (2) adding a safety layer on top of the nominal (learned locomotion) controller that leverages this learned residual model via a stochastic discrete-time CBF formulation enforcing trajectory-long safety constraints in probability. The result is a minimally-invasive safety layer that can be added to the existing autonomy stack to improve user command tracking and provide probabilistic safety guarantees. In hardware experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid, SHIELD enables safe navigation (obstacle avoidance) through varied indoor and outdoor environments using a nominal (unknown) RL controller and onboard perception.
39. Adversarial Locomotion and Motion Imitation for Humanoid Policy Learning
类人策略学习的对抗运动和运动模仿
人类展现出多样且富有表现力的全身运动。然而，在类人机器人中实现类似人类的全身协调仍具挑战性，因为模仿全身运动的传统方法往往忽略了上下身的不同角色。这种忽视导致策略学习计算成本高昂，并在真实场景执行中频繁引发机器人不稳定与跌倒。
为解决上述问题，我们提出对抗性运动与动作模仿（ALMI）框架，这一新型架构支持上下身之间的对抗策略学习。具体而言，下身旨在提供稳健的运动能力以跟随速度指令，同时上身跟踪各类动作；反之，上身策略确保机器人执行基于速度的运动时实现有效动作跟踪。通过迭代更新，这些策略实现了全身协调控制，并可通过遥操作系统扩展至移动操作任务。大量实验表明，我们的方法在仿真环境及全尺寸宇树 H1 机器人上均实现了稳健的运动控制与精确的动作跟踪。此外，我们发布了大规模全身运动控制数据集，其中包含可部署于实体机器人的MuJoCo仿真高质量片段化轨迹。
Humans exhibit diverse and expressive whole-body movements. However, attaining human-like whole-body coordination in humanoid robots remains challenging, as conventional approaches that mimic whole-body motions often neglect the distinct roles of upper and lower body. This oversight leads to computationally intensive policy learning and frequently causes robot instability and falls during real-world execution. To address these issues, we propose Adversarial Locomotion and Motion Imitation (ALMI), a novel framework that enables adversarial policy learning between upper and lower body. Specifically, the lower body aims to provide robust locomotion capabilities to follow velocity commands while the upper body tracks various motions. Conversely, the upper-body policy ensures effective motion tracking when the robot executes velocity-based movements. Through iterative updates, these policies achieve coordinated whole-body control, which can be extended to loco-manipulation tasks with teleoperation systems. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves robust locomotion and precise motion tracking in both simulation and on the full-size Unitree H1 robot. Additionally, we release a large-scale whole-body motion control dataset featuring high-quality episodic trajectories from MuJoCo simulations deployable on real robots.
40. FALCON: Learning Force-Adaptive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
猎鹰：学习力自适应人形机器人操纵
类人机器人移动操作在日常服务与工业任务中具有变革性潜力，然而实现具备三维末端执行器力交互的精确、稳健全身控制仍是重大挑战。现有方法通常局限于轻负载任务或四足 / 轮式平台。为克服这些局限，我们提出 FALCON—— 一种基于双智能体强化学习的框架，用于实现鲁棒的力自适应类人机器人移动操作。
FALCON 将全身控制分解为两个专用智能体：（1）下肢智能体，确保在外力干扰下的稳定运动；（2）上肢智能体，通过隐式自适应力补偿精确跟踪末端执行器位置。这两个智能体在仿真中通过力训练课程联合训练，该课程在遵守扭矩限制的同时，逐步提升施加于末端执行器的外力幅度。实验表明，与基线方法相比，FALCON实现了两倍精度的上肢关节跟踪，同时在外力干扰下维持稳健运动并实现更快的训练收敛。此外，FALCON支持无需特定实体奖励或课程调参的策略训练。使用相同训练配置，我们获得了可部署于多种类人机器人的策略，使其能够在真实场景中完成力交互移动操作任务，如负载运输（0-20N 力）、拉车（0-100N）和开门（0-40N）。
Humanoid loco-manipulation holds transformative potential for daily service and industrial tasks, yet achieving precise, robust whole-body control with 3D end-effector force interaction remains a major challenge. Prior approaches are often limited to lightweight tasks or quadrupedal/wheeled platforms. To overcome these limitations, we propose FALCON, a dual-agent reinforcement-learning-based framework for robust force-adaptive humanoid loco-manipulation. FALCON decomposes whole-body control into two specialized agents: (1) a lower-body agent ensuring stable locomotion under external force disturbances, and (2) an upper-body agent precisely tracking end-effector positions with implicit adaptive force compensation. These two agents are jointly trained in simulation with a force curriculum that progressively escalates the magnitude of external force exerted on the end effector while respecting torque limits. Experiments demonstrate that, compared to the baselines, FALCON achieves 2x more accurate upper-body joint tracking, while maintaining robust locomotion under force disturbances and achieving faster training convergence. Moreover, FALCON enables policy training without embodiment-specific reward or curriculum tuning. Using the same training setup, we obtain policies that are deployed across multiple humanoids, enabling forceful loco-manipulation tasks such as transporting payloads (0-20N force), cart-pulling (0-100N), and door-opening (0-40N) in the real world.
41. StyleLoco: Generative Adversarial Distillation for Natural Humanoid Robot Locomotion
StyleLoco：用于自然类人机器人运动的生成对抗蒸馏方法
类人机器人有望在不同速度和地形中实现自然运动的同时，获得广泛的移动能力。现有类人机器人运动学习方法面临一个根本性矛盾：基于手工设计奖励的强化学习可实现敏捷运动，但会产生不自然步态；而基于动作捕捉数据的生成对抗模仿学习（GAIL）虽能生成自然动作，却存在训练过程不稳定、敏捷性受限的问题。由于专家策略与人体运动数据集之间存在固有异质性，整合这些方法颇具挑战。
为此，我们提出 StyleLoco—— 一种通过生成对抗蒸馏（GAD）过程弥合这一差距的新型两阶段框架。该框架首先通过强化学习训练教师策略以实现敏捷动态的运动能力，随后采用多判别器架构，通过不同判别器同时从教师策略和动作捕捉数据中提取技能。这种方法有效结合了强化学习的敏捷性与类人运动的自然流畅性，同时缓解了对抗训练中常见的不稳定性问题。通过大量仿真与真实实验验证，StyleLoco 使类人机器人能够以专家训练策略的精准度和人体运动的自然美感执行多样化移动任务，成功实现了不同运动类型间的风格迁移，同时在广泛的指令输入下保持运动稳定性。
Humanoid robots are anticipated to acquire a wide range of locomotion capabilities while ensuring natural movement across varying speeds and terrains. Existing methods encounter a fundamental dilemma in learning humanoid locomotion: reinforcement learning with handcrafted rewards can achieve agile locomotion but produces unnatural gaits, while Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (GAIL) with motion capture data yields natural movements but suffers from unstable training processes and restricted agility. Integrating these approaches proves challenging due to the inherent heterogeneity between expert policies and human motion datasets. To address this, we introduce StyleLoco, a novel two-stage framework that bridges this gap through a Generative Adversarial Distillation (GAD) process. Our framework begins by training a teacher policy using reinforcement learning to achieve agile and dynamic locomotion. It then employs a multi-discriminator architecture, where distinct discriminators concurrently extract skills from both the teacher policy and motion capture data. This approach effectively combines the agility of reinforcement learning with the natural fluidity of human-like movements while mitigating the instability issues commonly associated with adversarial training. Through extensive simulation and real-world experiments, we demonstrate that StyleLoco enables humanoid robots to perform diverse locomotion tasks with the precision of expertly trained policies and the natural aesthetics of human motion, successfully transferring styles across different movement types while maintaining stable locomotion across a broad spectrum of command inputs.
42. Gait-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Phase Curriculum for Humanoid Locomotion
步态条件强化学习与人体运动多阶段课程
我们提出了一种统一的步态条件强化学习框架，使类人机器人能够在单一循环策略中执行站立、行走、奔跑及平滑过渡动作。一种紧凑的奖励路由机制基于独热步态标识动态激活特定步态目标，从而缓解奖励干扰并支持稳定的多步态学习。受人类启发的奖励项可促进生物力学上自然的运动模式，例如直膝支撑和协调的手臂 - 腿部摆动，且无需动作捕捉数据。结构化课程分阶段逐步引入步态复杂度并扩展指令空间。在仿真环境中，该策略成功实现了稳健的站立、行走、奔跑及步态过渡。在真实的宇树 G1 类人机器人上，我们验证了站立、行走及从行走到站立的过渡，展示了稳定且协调的 locomotion（运动控制）。这项工作为跨多种模式和环境的通用化、自然化类人机器人控制提供了可扩展的无参考解决方案。
We present a unified gait-conditioned reinforcement learning framework that enables humanoid robots to perform standing, walking, running, and smooth transitions within a single recurrent policy. A compact reward routing mechanism dynamically activates gait-specific objectives based on a one-hot gait ID, mitigating reward interference and supporting stable multi-gait learning. Human-inspired reward terms promote biomechanically natural motions, such as straight-knee stance and coordinated arm-leg swing, without requiring motion capture data. A structured curriculum progressively introduces gait complexity and expands command space over multiple phases. In simulation, the policy successfully achieves robust standing, walking, running, and gait transitions. On the real Unitree G1 humanoid, we validate standing, walking, and walk-to-stand transitions, demonstrating stable and coordinated locomotion. This work provides a scalable, reference-free solution toward versatile and naturalistic humanoid control across diverse modes and environments.
43. AMO: Adaptive Motion Optimization for Hyper-Dexterous Humanoid Whole-Body Control
AMO：面向高灵巧类人机器人全身控制的自适应运动优化
我们提出，类人机器人的高灵巧性很大程度上源于其高灵巧全身运动，这使其能够完成需要大操作空间的任务（如从地面拾取物体）。然而，由于类人机器人具有高自由度（DoF）和非线性动力学特性，在真实机器人上实现这些能力仍具挑战性。为此，我们提出了自适应运动优化（AMO）框架，该框架将仿真到现实强化学习（RL）与轨迹优化相结合，实现实时自适应全身控制。为缓解运动模仿强化学习中的分布偏差问题，我们构建了混合 AMO 数据集，并训练了一个能够对潜在分布外（O.O.D.）指令进行稳健按需自适应的网络。我们在仿真环境和 29 自由度宇树 G1 类人机器人上对 AMO 进行了验证，结果表明，与强基线方法相比，AMO 具有更强的稳定性和更大的操作空间。最后，我们证明 AMO 的稳定性能可通过模仿学习支持自主任务执行，突显了该系统的通用性和鲁棒性。
Humanoid robots derive much of their dexterity from hyper-dexterous whole-body movements, enabling tasks that require a large operational workspace: such as picking objects off the ground. However, achieving these capabilities on real humanoids remains challenging due to their high degrees of freedom (DoF) and nonlinear dynamics. We propose Adaptive Motion Optimization (AMO), a framework that integrates sim-to-real reinforcement learning (RL) with trajectory optimization for real-time, adaptive whole-body control. To mitigate distribution bias in motion imitation RL, we construct a hybrid AMO dataset and train a network capable of robust, on-demand adaptation to potentially O.O.D. commands. We validate AMO in simulation and on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrating superior stability and an expanded workspace compared to strong baselines. Finally, we show that AMO's consistent performance supports autonomous task execution via imitation learning, underscoring the system's versatility and robustness.
44. LangWBC: Language-directed Humanoid Whole-Body Control via End-to-end Learning
LangWBC：基于端到端学习的语言导向类人机器人全身控制
通用型类人机器人有望与人类进行直观交互，从而无缝融入日常生活。自然语言为此提供了最易使用的媒介。然而，将语言转化为类人机器人的全身动作仍是重大挑战，主要原因在于语言理解与物理动作之间存在鸿沟。在本研究中，我们提出了一种面向真实类人机器人全身控制的端到端语言导向策略。我们的方法将强化学习与策略蒸馏相结合，使单个神经网络能够直接解析语言指令并执行相应的物理动作。为增强动作多样性和组合性，我们融入了条件变分自动编码器（CVAE）结构。最终得到的策略可基于语言输入实现敏捷且多样化的全身行为，并在各种动作间实现平滑过渡，从而适应语言变体并生成新型动作。我们通过大量仿真实验和真实世界实验验证了该方法的有效性和泛化能力，展现了稳健的全身控制性能。
General-purpose humanoid robots are expected to interact intuitively with humans, enabling seamless integration into daily life. Natural language provides the most accessible medium for this purpose. However, translating language into humanoid whole-body motion remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the gap between linguistic understanding and physical actions. In this work, we present an end-to-end, language-directed policy for real-world humanoid whole-body control. Our approach combines reinforcement learning with policy distillation, allowing a single neural network to interpret language commands and execute corresponding physical actions directly. To enhance motion diversity and compositionality, we incorporate a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) structure. The resulting policy achieves agile and versatile whole-body behaviors conditioned on language inputs, with smooth transitions between various motions, enabling adaptation to linguistic variations and the emergence of novel motions. We validate the efficacy and generalizability of our method through extensive simulations and real-world experiments, demonstrating robust whole-body control.
45. H2-COMPACT: Human-Humanoid Co-Manipulation via Adaptive Contact Trajectory Policies
H2-COMPACT：基于自适应接触轨迹策略的人类 - 类人机器人协同操作
我们提出了一种分层策略学习框架，使类人机器人能够仅通过触觉线索推断人类意图，与人类伙伴协同搬运长尺寸负载。在上层，轻量级行为克隆网络处理来自双腕部传感器的六轴力 / 力矩数据流，输出反映引导者施力意图的全身平面速度指令。在下层，深度强化学习策略（在 Isaac Gym 中经随机负载（0-3 千克）和摩擦条件训练，并在 MuJoCo 及真实宇树 G1 机器人上验证）将这些高层速度指令映射为稳定的负载关节轨迹。通过将意图解释（力→速度）与足式运动（速度→关节）解耦，我们的方法兼具对人类输入的直观响应能力和负载自适应行走的鲁棒性。我们在无动作捕捉或标记的条件下收集训练数据，仅使用同步 RGB 视频和力 / 力矩读数，借助 SAM2 和 WHAM 算法提取三维人体姿态和速度。在真实场景测试中，我们的类人机器人在协同搬运任务中的表现（完成时间、轨迹偏差、速度同步性和跟随力）达到蒙眼人类跟随者的基准水平。这项工作首次展示了触觉引导与全身足式控制的融合学习，实现流畅的人机协同操作。代码和视频可在 H2-COMPACT 网站获取。
We present a hierarchical policy-learning framework that enables a legged humanoid to cooperatively carry extended loads with a human partner using only haptic cues for intent inference. At the upper tier, a lightweight behavior-cloning network consumes six-axis force/torque streams from dual wrist-mounted sensors and outputs whole-body planar velocity commands that capture the leader's applied forces. At the lower tier, a deep-reinforcement-learning policy, trained under randomized payloads (0-3 kg) and friction conditions in Isaac Gym and validated in MuJoCo and on a real Unitree G1, maps these high-level twists to stable, under-load joint trajectories. By decoupling intent interpretation (force -> velocity) from legged locomotion (velocity -> joints), our method combines intuitive responsiveness to human inputs with robust, load-adaptive walking. We collect training data without motion-capture or markers, only synchronized RGB video and F/T readings, employing SAM2 and WHAM to extract 3D human pose and velocity. In real-world trials, our humanoid achieves cooperative carry-and-move performance (completion time, trajectory deviation, velocity synchrony, and follower-force) on par with a blindfolded human-follower baseline. This work is the first to demonstrate learned haptic guidance fused with full-body legged control for fluid human-humanoid co-manipulation. Code and videos are available on the H2-COMPACT website.
46. HuB: Learning Extreme Humanoid Balance
HuB：学习极端类人平衡
我们提出 HuB（类人机器人平衡控制）框架，该框架集成了参考运动优化、平衡感知策略学习和仿真到现实鲁棒性训练，各组件针对性解决三大核心挑战：参考运动误差导致的不稳定性、形态不匹配引发的学习困难，以及传感器噪声和未建模动力学造成的仿真 - 现实鸿沟。人体展现出卓越的运动能力 —— 如单脚稳定站立或以超过 1.5 米的高度完成高踢腿动作 —— 这些均需精确的平衡控制。尽管近期类人机器人控制研究已借助强化学习追踪人体运动以实现技能获取，但将该范式应用于高平衡需求任务仍具挑战性。我们在宇树 G1 类人机器人上针对挑战性准静态平衡任务进行了验证，包括 “燕式平衡” 和 “李小龙踢腿” 等极端单腿姿势。即使在强力物理干扰（如用力踢击）下，我们的策略仍保持稳定，而基线方法始终无法完成这些任务。
The human body demonstrates exceptional motor capabilities-such as standing steadily on one foot or performing a high kick with the leg raised over 1.5 meters-both requiring precise balance control. While recent research on humanoid control has leveraged reinforcement learning to track human motions for skill acquisition, applying this paradigm to balance-intensive tasks remains challenging. In this work, we identify three key obstacles: instability from reference motion errors, learning difficulties due to morphological mismatch, and the sim-to-real gap caused by sensor noise and unmodeled dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose HuB (Humanoid Balance), a unified framework that integrates reference motion refinement, balance-aware policy learning, and sim-to-real robustness training, with each component targeting a specific challenge. We validate our approach on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot across challenging quasi-static balance tasks, including extreme single-legged poses such as Swallow Balance and Bruce Lee's Kick. Our policy remains stable even under strong physical disturbances-such as a forceful soccer strike-while baseline methods consistently fail to complete these tasks.
47.KungfuBot: Physics-Based Humanoid Whole-Body Control for Learning Highly-Dynamic SkillsKungfuBot：基于物理的人形机器人全身控制以学习高动态技能

Humanoid robots are promising to acquire various skills by imitating human behaviors. However, existing algorithms are only capable of tracking smooth, low - speed human motions, even with delicate reward and curriculum design. Our method achieves significantly lower tracking errors than existing approaches and is successfully deployed on the Unitree G1 robot, demonstrating stable and expressive behaviors. 48. Hierarchical Vision-Language Planning for Multi-Step Humanoid Manipulation
用于多步人形机器人操作的分层视觉-语言规划
人形机器人能够可靠执行复杂多步操作任务对其在工业和家庭环境中的有效部署至关重要。本文提出一种分层规划与控制框架，旨在实现可靠的多步人形机器人操作。该系统包含三层结构：（1）基于强化学习的底层控制器，负责跟踪全身运动目标；（2）通过模仿学习训练的中层技能策略集，为任务的不同阶段生成运动目标；（3）高层视觉-语言规划模块，利用预训练视觉语言模型（VLM）确定应执行的技能并实时监控其完成状态。实验在宇树G1人形机器人上进行非抓取式拾取放置任务验证。在40次真实场景测试中，该分层系统完成完整操作序列的成功率达72.5%。实验证实了所提分层框架的可行性，凸显了基于VLM的技能规划与监控在多步操作场景中的优势。策略执行演示视频详见https://vlp-humanoid.github.io/。
Enabling humanoid robots to reliably execute complex multi-step manipulation tasks is crucial for their effective deployment in industrial and household environments. This paper presents a hierarchical planning and control framework designed to achieve reliable multi-step humanoid manipulation. The proposed system comprises three layers: (1) a low-level RL-based controller responsible for tracking whole-body motion targets; (2) a mid-level set of skill policies trained via imitation learning that produce motion targets for different steps of a task; and (3) a high-level vision-language planning module that determines which skills should be executed and also monitors their completion in real-time using pretrained vision-language models (VLMs). Experimental validation is performed on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot executing a non-prehensile pick-and-place task. Over 40 real-world trials, the hierarchical system achieved a 72.5% success rate in completing the full manipulation sequence. These experiments confirm the feasibility of the proposed hierarchical system, highlighting the benefits of VLM-based skill planning and monitoring for multi-step manipulation scenarios. 49. Preferenced Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies for Dynamic Bipedal Loco-Manipulation
用于动态双足移动操作的偏好性 oracle 引导多模式策略
动态移动操作需要全身控制以及与物体和环境的丰富接触交互。现有基于学习的方法通常训练高层策略或手工设计有限状态机，以在独立训练的低层技能策略间切换，这往往导致准静态行为。我们提出偏好神谕引导多模式策略（Preferenced Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies），通过学习单一策略来掌握多种模式及其偏好转换序列。通过将混合自动机设计为神谕以生成不同控制模式的参考信号，并通过有界探索引导策略优化。借助与任务无关的偏好奖励，强制学习所需的模式转换序列，从而有效解决任务。在全向推箱和足球等单物体移动操作任务中，我们的方法实现了全身控制和平滑过渡，支持运球、射门和停球等丰富接触动作。利用神谕的抽象能力，我们使用相同的奖励定义和权重，在HECTOR V1、伯克利人形机器人、宇树G1和H1等多种机器人形态上解决了各类移动操作任务。项目网站：https://indweller.github.io/ogmplm/
Dynamic loco-manipulation requires whole-body control and contact-rich interactions with objects and the environment. Existing learning-based approaches train a high-level policy or hand-design a finite state machine to switch between low-level skill policies trained independently, often resulting in quasi-static behaviors. We propose Preferenced Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies to learn a single policy that masters multiple modes and their preferred sequences of transitions. Designing hybrid automatons as oracles to generate references over different control modes, policy optimization is guided through bounded exploration. With a task-agnostic preference reward, we enforce learning a desired sequence of mode transitions, thereby solving the task effectively. In uni-object loco-manipulation tasks like omnidirectional box moving and soccer, our approach results in whole-body control and smooth transitions, enabling contact-rich dribbling, goal kicks, and ball stops. Leveraging the oracle's abstraction, we solve each loco-manipulation task across diverse robot morphologies, including HECTOR V1, Berkeley Humanoid, Unitree G1, and H1, using the same reward definition and weights. 50. DoublyAware: Dual Planning and Policy Awareness for Temporal Difference Learning in Humanoid Locomotion
DoublyAware：用于人形机器人运动时序差分学习的双重规划与策略感知方法
实现人形机器人运动的鲁棒性学习是基于模型的强化学习（MBRL）的核心挑战，环境随机性与不确定性会阻碍高效探索和学习稳定性。在具有复杂接触动力学的高维动作空间中，环境的偶然不确定性（aleatoric uncertainty）可能被放大，并在学习阶段与模型中的认知不确定性（epistemic uncertainty）进一步纠缠。为此，我们提出 DoublyAware—— 一种时序差分模型预测控制（TD-MPC）的不确定性感知扩展方法，其将不确定性显式分解为两个独立可解释的分量：规划不确定性与策略不确定性。
为处理规划不确定性，DoublyAware 采用共形预测（conformal prediction）通过分位数校准的风险边界过滤候选轨迹，确保统计一致性和对随机动力学的鲁棒性；同时，策略展开（policy rollouts）被用作结构化先验信息，通过组相对策略约束（GRPC）优化器在潜在动作空间中施加基于分组的自适应信任区域，支撑学习阶段。这种原理性结合使机器人智能体能够优先选择高置信度、高奖励行为，同时在不确定性下维持有效定向探索。
在 HumanoidBench 运动套件中基于宇树 26 自由度 H1-2 人形机器人的实验表明，相比强化学习基线方法，DoublyAware 实现了更高的样本效率、更快的收敛速度和更强的运动可行性。仿真结果强调了结构化不确定性建模在基于 TD-MPC 的人形机器人运动学习中对数据高效性和决策可靠性的重要意义。
Achieving robust robot learning for humanoid locomotion is a fundamental challenge in model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), where environmental stochasticity and randomness can hinder efficient exploration and learning stability. The environmental, so-called aleatoric, uncertainty can be amplified in high-dimensional action spaces with complex contact dynamics, and further entangled with epistemic uncertainty in the models during learning phases. In this work, we propose DoublyAware, an uncertainty-aware extension of Temporal Difference Model Predictive Control (TD-MPC) that explicitly decomposes uncertainty into two disjoint interpretable components, i.e., planning and policy uncertainties. To handle the planning uncertainty, DoublyAware employs conformal prediction to filter candidate trajectories using quantile-calibrated risk bounds, ensuring statistical consistency and robustness against stochastic dynamics. Meanwhile, policy rollouts are leveraged as structured informative priors to support the learning phase with Group-Relative Policy Constraint (GRPC) optimizers that impose a group-based adaptive trust-region in the latent action space. This principled combination enables the robot agent to prioritize high-confidence, high-reward behavior while maintaining effective, targeted exploration under uncertainty. Evaluated on the HumanoidBench locomotion suite with the Unitree 26-DoF H1-2 humanoid, DoublyAware demonstrates improved sample efficiency, accelerated convergence, and enhanced motion feasibility compared to RL baselines. Our simulation results emphasize the significance of structured uncertainty modeling for data-efficient and reliable decision-making in TD-MPC-based humanoid locomotion learning.
51. Hold My Beer: Learning Gentle Humanoid Locomotion and End-Effector Stabilization Control
帮我拿好啤酒：学习仿人机器人的平稳移动与末端执行器稳定控制
你的仿人机器人能走上前，递给你一杯满杯的啤酒 —— 且一滴不洒吗？尽管仿人机器人越来越多地出现在花哨的演示中 —— 跳舞、送包裹、穿越崎岖地形 —— 但移动过程中的精细控制仍是一大挑战。特别是，行走时稳定装载物品的末端执行器（EE）问题远未解决，这源于任务动态特性的根本不匹配：移动需要慢时间尺度的鲁棒控制，而末端执行器稳定则需要快速、高精度的修正。
为此，我们提出了 SoFTA（快慢双智能体框架），该框架将上半身和下半身控制解耦为两个独立的智能体，以不同频率运行并采用不同的奖励机制。这种时间与目标上的分离减少了策略干扰，实现了协调的全身行为。SoFTA 以上半身 100Hz 的频率执行动作以实现精确的末端执行器控制，以下半身 50Hz 的频率执行动作以保证稳健的步态。
与基线方法相比，它将末端执行器的加速度降低了 2-5 倍，稳定性更接近人类水平，能够完成精细任务，例如搬运近乎满杯的容器、移动时拍摄稳定视频，以及在保持末端执行器稳定的同时抵御干扰。我们在宇树 G1 和 Booster T1 机器人上对 SoFTA 进行了验证，结果表明其具有很强的跨平台通用性。
Can your humanoid walk up and hand you a full cup of beer—without spilling a drop? While humanoids are increasingly featured in flashy demos—dancing, delivering packages, traversing rough terrain—fine-grained control during locomotion remains a significant challenge. In particular, stabilizing a filled end-effector (EE) while walking is far from solved, due to a fundamental mismatch in task dynamics: locomotion demands slow-timescale, robust control, whereas EE stabilization requires rapid, high-precision corrections. To address this, we propose SoFTA , a Slow-Fast Two-Agent framework that decouples upper-body and lower-body control into separate agents operating at different frequencies and with distinct rewards. This temporal and objective separation mitigates policy interference and enables coordinated whole-body behavior. SoFTA executes upper-body actions at 100 Hz for precise EE control and lower-body actions at 50 Hz for robust gait. It reduces EE acceleration by 2-5x to baselines and performs much closer to human-level stability, enabling delicate tasks such as carrying nearly full cups, capturing steady video during locomotion, and disturbance rejection with EE stability. We validate SoFTA on both Unitree G1 and Booster T1, showing strong cross-platform generalizatin.
52. Learning Robust Motion Skills via Critical Adversarial Attacks for Humanoid Robots
基于关键对抗攻击的仿人机器人鲁棒运动技能学习
仿人机器人在日常任务中展现出巨大潜力。然而，基于强化学习的运动策略常因仿真与现实的动力学差距导致鲁棒性下降，进而影响实体机器人的灵活性。在本研究中，我们提出一种新型鲁棒对抗训练范式，旨在增强仿人机器人运动策略在现实世界中的鲁棒性。该范式引入一个可学习的对抗攻击网络，能够精准识别运动策略中的薄弱环节并施加针对性扰动，通过动态对抗训练迫使运动策略提升对扰动的抵抗能力。
