In this study, we propose an anisotropic Lipschitz-constrained policy (ALCP) that maps a task-space stiffness upper bound to a state-dependent Lipschitz-style constraint on the policy Jacobian. The resulting constraint is enforced during RL training via a hinge-squared spectral-norm penalty, preserving physical interpretability while enabling direction-dependent compliance. Experiments on Unitree G1 humanoid robots show that ALCP improves locomotion stability and impact robustness, while reducing oscillations and energy usage.
ULTRA: Unified Multimodal Control for Autonomous Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
ULTRA：用于自主人形机器人全身运动操控的统一多模态控制
实现自主且通用的全身运动-操作能力，仍然是类人机器人走向实际应用的核心瓶颈。然而，现有方法从根本上受到多重限制：重定向数据往往稀缺或质量不高；方法难以扩展到大规模技能库；更重要的是，它们依赖于跟踪预定义的运动参考，而非基于感知和高层任务指令生成行为。为应对这些问题，我们提出了 ULTRA，一个包含两个关键组件的统一框架。首先，我们引入了一种由物理驱动的神经重定向算法，可将大规模动作捕捉数据映射到类人机器人形态，同时在富含接触的交互中保持物理合理性。其次，我们学习了一个统一的多模态控制器，既支持密集参考，也支持稀疏任务规格，并能够处理从高精度动作捕捉状态到带噪声的自中心视觉输入等多种感知形式。我们将一个通用的跟踪策略蒸馏进该控制器，将运动技能压缩到紧凑的潜在空间中，并通过强化学习微调来扩展能力覆盖范围、提升在分布外场景下的鲁棒性。这使得系统无需测试时的参考动作，也能从稀疏意图生成协调的全身行为。我们在仿真环境和真实的 Unitree G1 类人机器人上对 ULTRA 进行了评估，结果表明，该方法能够从自中心感知中实现面向目标的自主全身运动-操作，并在技能受限的纯跟踪基线方法上取得了稳定的性能提升。
Achieving autonomous and versatile whole-body loco-manipulation remains a central barrier to making humanoids practically useful. Yet existing approaches are fundamentally constrained: retargeted data are often scarce or low-quality; methods struggle to scale to large skill repertoires; and, most importantly, they rely on tracking predefined motion references rather than generating behavior from perception and high-level task specifications. To address these limitations, we propose ULTRA, a unified framework with two key components. First, we introduce a physics-driven neural retargeting algorithm that translates large-scale motion capture to humanoid embodiments while preserving physical plausibility for contact-rich interactions. Second, we learn a unified multimodal controller that supports both dense references and sparse task specifications, under sensing ranging from accurate motion-capture state to noisy egocentric visual inputs. We distill a universal tracking policy into this controller, compress motor skills into a compact latent space, and apply reinforcement learning finetuning to expand coverage and improve robustness under out-of-distribution scenarios. This enables coordinated whole-body behavior from sparse intent without test-time reference motions. We evaluate ULTRA in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid. Results show that ULTRA generalizes to autonomous, goal-conditioned whole-body loco-manipulation from egocentric perception, consistently outperforming tracking-only baselines with limited skills.
SteadyTray: Learning Object Balancing Tasks in Humanoid Tray Transport via Residual Reinforcement Learning
SteadyTray：通过残差强化学习学习人形机器人托盘运输中的物体平衡任务
在非结构化环境中，如何在动态双足行走固有振荡的影响下稳定未固定负载，仍是制约类人机器人发展的关键工程瓶颈。为解决这一问题，我们提出了 ReST-RL，一种分层强化学习架构，并通过 SteadyTray 基准进行评估。该方法显式地将行走控制与负载稳定解耦：不同于单体端到端学习框架，我们将稳健的基础行走策略与一个动态残差模块相结合，后者专门用于在末端执行器处主动抵消由步态引起的扰动。这种架构上的分离在不削弱双足稳定性的前提下，实现了托盘运输的高稳定性。在仿真中，该残差设计在步态平滑性和姿态精度方面显著优于端到端基线，在变速跟踪任务中取得了 96.9% 的成功率，并在外力扰动下实现了 74.5% 的鲁棒性。该方法已成功部署于 Unitree G1 类人机器人硬件上，展现出在不同物体及外力干扰条件下高度可靠的零样本仿真到现实迁移能力。
Stabilizing unsecured payloads against the inherent oscillations of dynamic bipedal locomotion remains a critical engineering bottleneck for humanoids in unstructured environments. To solve this, we introduce ReST-RL, a hierarchical reinforcement learning architecture that explicitly decouples locomotion from payload stabilization, evaluated via the SteadyTray benchmark. Rather than relying on monolithic end-to-end learning, our framework integrates a robust base locomotion policy with a dynamic residual module engineered to actively cancel gait-induced perturbations at the end-effector. This architectural separation ensures steady tray transport without degrading the underlying bipedal stability. In simulation, the residual design significantly outperforms end-to-end baselines in gait smoothness and orientation accuracy, achieving a 96.9% success rate in variable velocity tracking and 74.5% robustness against external force disturbances. Successfully deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid hardware, this modular approach demonstrates highly reliable zero-shot sim-to-real generalization across various objects and external force disturbances.
GeoLoco: Leveraging 3D Geometric Priors from Visual Foundation Model for Robust RGB-Only Humanoid Locomotion
GeoLoco：利用视觉基础模型中的 3D 几何先验信息实现鲁棒的仅 RGB 人形运动
当前具身类人运动感知的主流范式高度依赖主动深度传感器。然而，这种以深度为中心的方法从根本上丢弃了视觉世界中丰富的语义信息与稠密外观线索，使底层控制与实现通用具身智能所需的高层推理相割裂。尽管单目 RGB 提供了一种无处不在且信息密集的替代方案，但直接从原始二维像素进行端到端强化学习会面临极低的样本效率，以及由于几何尺度缺失而导致的灾难性“仿真到现实”迁移失败。为打破这一僵局，我们提出 GeoLoco，一个完全基于 RGB 的运动框架，通过利用一个冻结的、具备尺度感知能力的视觉基础模型（VFM）的强大几何先验，将单目图像建模为高维三维潜在表示。不同于简单的特征拼接，我们设计了一种基于本体感知查询的多头交叉注意力机制，使系统能够根据机器人实时步态相位，动态关注与任务关键相关的拓扑特征。关键在于，为防止策略对表面纹理产生过拟合，我们引入了一种双头辅助学习机制，这种显式正则化约束高维潜在空间必须严格对齐于真实地形几何，从而保证了稳健的零样本仿真到现实迁移能力。GeoLoco 完全在仿真中训练，并成功实现向 Unitree G1 类人机器人的零样本迁移，在复杂地形中展现出可靠的通过能力。
The prevailing paradigm of perceptive humanoid locomotion relies heavily on active depth sensors. However, this depth-centric approach fundamentally discards the rich semantic and dense appearance cues of the visual world, severing low-level control from the high-level reasoning essential for general embodied intelligence. While monocular RGB offers a ubiquitous, information-dense alternative, end-to-end reinforcement learning from raw 2D pixels suffers from extreme sample inefficiency and catastrophic sim-to-real collapse due to the inherent loss of geometric scale. To break this deadlock, we propose GeoLoco, a purely RGB-driven locomotion framework that conceptualizes monocular images as high-dimensional 3D latent representations by harnessing the powerful geometric priors of a frozen, scale-aware Visual Foundation Model (VFM). Rather than naive feature concatenation, we design a proprioceptive-query multi-head cross-attention mechanism that dynamically attends to task-critical topological features conditioned on the robot's real-time gait phase. Crucially, to prevent the policy from overfitting to superficial textures, we introduce a dual-head auxiliary learning scheme. This explicit regularization forces the high-dimensional latent space to strictly align with the physical terrain geometry, ensuring robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. Trained exclusively in simulation, GeoLoco achieves robust zero-shot transfer to the Unitree G1 humanoid and successfully negotiates challenging terrains.
STRIDE: Structured Lagrangian and Stochastic Residual Dynamics via Flow Matching
STRIDE：基于流匹配的结构化拉格朗日和随机残差动力学
在非结构化环境中运行的机器人系统必须应对由间歇接触、摩擦变化以及未建模柔顺性带来的显著不确定性。尽管近年来无模型方法已展现出令人瞩目的性能，但在许多实际部署场景中，仍然需要能够支持规划、约束处理与在线适应的预测模型。解析刚体模型具备良好的物理结构，但往往难以刻画复杂的交互效应；而纯数据驱动模型则可能违背物理一致性、产生数据偏置，并在长时预测中累积漂移。为此，我们提出 STRIDE，一种动力学学习框架，将守恒的刚体力学与具有不确定性、可视为随机性的非守恒交互效应进行显式分离。其中，结构化部分采用拉格朗日神经网络（LNN）建模，以保持能量一致的惯性动力学；残余的交互力则通过条件流匹配（CFM）进行表示，以捕捉多模态的交互现象。两部分以端到端方式联合训练，使模型在保留物理结构的同时，能够表达复杂的随机行为。我们在不同复杂度的系统上对 STRIDE 进行了评估，包括单摆、Unitree Go1 四足机器人以及 Unitree G1 类人机器人。结果表明，与确定性残差基线相比，该方法在长时预测误差上降低了 20%，在接触力预测误差上降低了 30%，从而在不确定机器人环境中支持更加可靠的基于模型的控制。
Robotic systems operating in unstructured environments must operate under significant uncertainty arising from intermittent contacts, frictional variability, and unmodeled compliance. While recent model-free approaches have demonstrated impressive performance, many deployment settings still require predictive models that support planning, constraint handling, and online adaptation. Analytical rigid-body models provide strong physical structure but often fail to capture complex interaction effects, whereas purely data-driven models may violate physical consistency, exhibit data bias, and accumulate long-horizon drift. In this work, we propose STRIDE, a dynamics learning framework that explicitly separates conservative rigid-body mechanics from uncertain, effectively stochastic non-conservative interaction effects. The structured component is modeled using a Lagrangian Neural Network (LNN) to preserve energy-consistent inertial dynamics, while residual interaction forces are represented using Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) to capture multi-modal interaction phenomena. The two components are trained jointly end-to-end, enabling the model to retain physical structure while representing complex stochastic behavior. We evaluate STRIDE on systems of increasing complexity, including a pendulum, the Unitree Go1 quadruped, and the Unitree G1 humanoid. Results show 20% reduction in long-horizon prediction error and 30% reduction in contact force prediction error compared to deterministic residual baselines, supporting more reliable model-based control in uncertain robotic environments.
SafeFlow: Real-Time Text-Driven Humanoid Whole-Body Control via Physics-Guided Rectified Flow and Selective Safety Gating
SafeFlow：基于物理引导的整流和选择性安全门控的实时文本驱动人形全身控制
近年来，实时交互式文本驱动的动作生成取得了显著进展，使类人机器人能够执行多样化行为。然而，仅基于运动学的生成方法往往会产生“物理幻觉”，生成的运动轨迹在物理上不可实现，难以被下游运动跟踪控制器稳定执行，甚至在真实环境中存在安全隐患。这些问题通常源于缺乏面向真实机器人执行的显式物理约束目标，并在分布外（OOD）用户输入下进一步加剧。为此，我们提出 SafeFlow，一种文本驱动的类人全身控制框架，将物理引导的动作生成与基于显式风险指标的三阶段安全门机制相结合。SafeFlow 采用两级架构：在高层，我们在 VAE 潜在空间中通过物理引导的校正流匹配（Physics-Guided Rectified Flow Matching）生成运动轨迹，以提升在真实机器人上的可执行性，并通过 Reflow 加速采样，减少函数评估次数（NFE），从而满足实时控制需求；三阶段安全门则实现选择性执行，包括在文本嵌入空间中利用马氏距离检测语义分布外提示、通过方向敏感性差异指标筛除不稳定生成结果，以及在将轨迹传递给低层运动跟踪控制器之前施加最终的硬性运动学约束（如关节与速度限制）。在 Unitree G1 上的大量实验表明，SafeFlow 在成功率、物理一致性和推理速度方面均优于以往基于扩散的方法，同时保持了良好的动作多样性与表达能力。
Recent advances in real-time interactive text-driven motion generation have enabled humanoids to perform diverse behaviors. However, kinematics-only generators often exhibit physical hallucinations, producing motion trajectories that are physically infeasible to track with a downstream motion tracking controller or unsafe for real-world deployment. These failures often arise from the lack of explicit physics-aware objectives for real-robot execution and become more severe under out-of-distribution (OOD) user inputs. Hence, we propose SafeFlow, a text-driven humanoid whole-body control framework that combines physics-guided motion generation with a 3-Stage Safety Gate driven by explicit risk indicators. SafeFlow adopts a two-level architecture. At the high level, we generate motion trajectories using Physics-Guided Rectified Flow Matching in a VAE latent space to improve real-robot executability, and further accelerate sampling via Reflow to reduce the number of function evaluations (NFE) for real-time control. The 3-Stage Safety Gate enables selective execution by detecting semantic OOD prompts using a Mahalanobis score in text-embedding space, filtering unstable generations via a directional sensitivity discrepancy metric, and enforcing final hard kinematic constraints such as joint and velocity limits before passing the generated trajectory to a low-level motion tracking controller. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that SafeFlow outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in success rate, physical compliance, and inference speed, while maintaining diverse expressiveness.
ADAPT: Adaptive Dual-projection Architecture for Perceptive Traversal
ADAPT：用于感知遍历的自适应双投影架构
在复杂三维环境中实现敏捷的类人运动，需要在感知精度与计算效率之间取得平衡，但现有方法通常依赖于固定的传感配置。为此，我们提出 ADAPT（自适应双投影感知架构），通过水平高程图表征地形几何信息，并利用垂直距离图刻画可通行空间约束。进一步地，ADAPT 将感知范围建模为一种可学习的动作，使策略能够在高速运动时扩展感知视野，而在环境拥挤时收缩感知范围以获得更精细的局部分辨率。与基于体素的基线方法相比，ADAPT 显著降低了观测维度与计算开销，同时大幅加快了训练过程。实验结果表明，该方法能够实现向 Unitree G1 类人机器人的零样本迁移，并显著优于固定感知范围的基线方法，在多样化三维环境挑战中展现出高度鲁棒的通行能力。
Agile humanoid locomotion in complex 3D en- vironments requires balancing perceptual fidelity with com- putational efficiency, yet existing methods typically rely on rigid sensing configurations. We propose ADAPT (Adaptive dual-projection architecture for perceptive traversal), which represents the environment using a horizontal elevation map for terrain geometry and a vertical distance map for traversable- space constraints. ADAPT further treats its spatial sensing range as a learnable action, enabling the policy to expand its perceptual horizon during fast motion and contract it in cluttered scenes for finer local resolution. Compared with voxel-based baselines, ADAPT drastically reduces observation dimensionality and computational overhead while substantially accelerating training. Experimentally, it achieves successful zero-shot transfer to a Unitree G1 Humanoid and signifi- cantly outperforms fixed-range baselines, yielding highly robust traversal across diverse 3D environtmental challenges.
Designing for Transparency in Human–Robot Interaction:A Dashboard and Custom Hardware for Mechanistic Interpretability
人机交互透明化设计：用于机制可解释性的仪表盘和定制硬件
随着具身智能系统从确定性自动化迈向由视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型驱动的流畅决策，这类“黑箱”系统的内在不透明性已成为实现安全、高效人机交互的重要障碍。本文认为，透明性不应作为事后补充，而应作为一项基础性设计约束，被整合进机器人的物理与数字架构之中。我们基于 Unitree G1 平台构建了一个类人机器人演示系统，以体现这一整体设计理念。该方案将定制工业硬件（包括配备“面部用户界面”（Face UI）用于社会信号表达的专用头部模块）与实时数字仪表盘相结合，后者能够将复杂的 AI 推理过程转化为自然语言，并可视化从感知到执行的全过程。为评估这种多层次透明性设计的有效性，我们开展了一项用户研究（N=10），将完整透明系统与缺乏社交界面和仪表盘的基线系统进行对比。结果表明，我们的架构显著提升了机器人在交互过程中的透明性与可理解性。这些发现表明，根据具体用户场景定制透明性机制，对于自主系统在共享人类空间中的成功部署至关重要。
As embodied AI systems transition from deterministic automation to fluid decision-making driven by systems such as VisionLanguage-Action (VLA) models, the inherent opacity of these "black box" systems creates significant barriers to safe and effective humanrobot interaction. This paper argues that transparency should not be a post-hoc addition, but a foundational design constraint integrated into the robot’s physical and digital architecture. We present a humanoid demonstrator built on the Unitree G1 platform that embodies this holistic design philosophy. Our approach combines custom industrial hardware, including a specialised head unit with a Face User Interface (Face UI) for social signaling, with a real-time digital dashboard that translates complex AI reasoning into natural language and visualises the perception-to-actuation pipeline. To evaluate the efficacy of this multi-layered transparency design, we conducted a user study (N=10) comparing the fully transparent system against a baseline lacking the social interface and dashboard. Results indicate that our architecture improved transparency and understandability of the robot during interaction. These findings suggest that tailoring transparency mechanisms to specific user contexts is critical for the successful deployment of autonomous systems in shared human spaces.
RoboForge: Physically Optimized Text-guided Whole-Body Locomotion for Humanoids
RoboForge：面向人形机器人的物理优化文本引导全身运动系统
尽管生成模型已能够根据文本生成类人运动，但将这些动作迁移到类人机器人上进行物理执行仍然充满挑战。现有流程通常受限于重定向过程，其中运动学质量常因物理不可行性、接触切换误差以及真实世界动力学数据成本高昂而受到影响。我们提出了一种统一的潜在驱动框架，通过一个无需重定向、以物理优化为核心的流程，将自然语言与类人全身运动连接起来。不同于将生成与控制视为彼此独立的阶段，我们的核心思想是在物理约束下对二者进行双向耦合，并引入物理合理性优化模块（PP-Opt）作为关键接口。在前向过程中，PP-Opt 通过以物理合理性为核心的奖励函数，对教师-学生蒸馏策略进行优化，从而抑制悬浮、滑移和穿透等伪影；在反向过程中，它将基于奖励优化得到的仿真轨迹转化为高质量的显式动作数据，用于微调动作生成器，使其学习到更加符合物理规律的潜在分布。这种双向设计形成了一个自我增强的循环：生成器学习具备物理约束的潜在空间，而控制器则学习在动力学一致性下执行由潜变量条件化的行为。在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上的实验表明，该双向优化方法显著提升了跟踪精度和任务成功率。在 IsaacLab 和 MuJoCo 环境中的结果也显示，这种隐式潜在驱动流程在精度和稳定性方面均持续优于传统的显式重定向基线。通过将基于扩散的动作生成与物理合理性优化相结合，我们的框架为可部署的文本驱动类人智能提供了一条切实可行的路径。
While generative models have become effective at producing human-like motions from text, transferring these motions to humanoid robots for physical execution remains challenging. Existing pipelines are often limited by retargeting, where kinematic quality is undermined by physical infeasibility, contact-transition errors, and the high cost of real-world dynamical data. We present a unified latent-driven framework that bridges natural language and whole-body humanoid locomotion through a retarget-free, physics-optimized pipeline. Rather than treating generation and control as separate stages, our key insight is to couple them bidirectionally under physical introduce a Physical Plausibility Optimization (PP-Opt) module as the coupling interface. In the forward direction, PP-Opt refines a teacher-student distillation policy with a plausibility-centric reward to suppress artifacts such as floating, skating, and penetration. In the backward direction, it converts reward-optimized simulation rollouts into high-quality explicit motion data, which is used to fine-tune the motion generator toward a more physically plausible latent distribution. This bidirectional design forms a self-improving cycle: the generator learns a physically grounded latent space, while the controller learns to execute latent-conditioned behaviors with dynamical experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid show that our bidirectional optimization improves tracking accuracy and success rates. Across IsaacLab and MuJoCo, the implicit latent-driven pipeline consistently outperforms conventional explicit retargeting baselines in both precision and stability. By coupling diffusion-based motion generation with physical plausibility optimization, our framework provides a practical path toward deployable text-guided humanoid intelligence.
Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery
人形机器人作为内窥镜手术的第一助手
类人机器人已成为技术发展的焦点，主流论述中甚至声称其将在数年内具备外科手术能力。然而，这些预测多停留在愿景层面，缺乏实证支撑。迄今为止，尚无类人机器人在真实手术中协助外科医生，更遑论独立完成手术。本文工作在这一背景下取得了突破性进展。我们报告了一项概念验证实验：通过遥操作控制的 Unitree G1 类人机器人在一例遗体蝶窦切除术中提供内窥镜可视化支持，由一名耳鼻喉科主治医师完成手术操作。手术顺利完成，且全过程保持了稳定的可视化效果。遥操作方式使我们能够评估类人机器人在外科辅助中是否具备满足体力与精度要求的形态优势，而认知层面的任务目前仍由人类操作者承担。术后分析识别了实现临床转化所需的关键工程改进方向，同时也指出了如自主诊断性内窥检查等近期应用机会。该研究验证了类人机器人在外科辅助中的形态可行性，并明确了未来持续发展的关键挑战。
Humanoid robots have become a focal point of technological ambition, with claims of surgical capability within years in mainstream discourse. These projections are aspirational yet lack empirical grounding. To date, no humanoid has assisted a surgeon through an actual procedure, let alone performed one. The work described here breaks this new ground. Here we report a proof of concept in which a teleoperated Unitree G1 provided endoscopic visualization while an attending otolaryngologist performed a cadaveric sphenoidectomy. The procedure was completed successfully, with stable visualization maintained throughout. Teleoperation allowed assessment of whether the humanoid form factor could meet the physical demands of surgical assistance in terms of sustenance and precision; the cognitive demands were satisfied -- for now -- by the operator. Post-procedure analysis identified engineering targets for clinical translation, alongside near-term opportunities such as autonomous diagnostic scoping. This work establishes form-factor feasibility for humanoid surgical assistance while identifying challenges for continued development.
CyboRacket: A Perception-to-Action Framework for Humanoid Racket Sports
CyboRacket：人形球拍运动的感知到行动框架
动态球类交互任务对机器人而言仍然极具挑战，因为它们要求在极短反应时间内实现紧密的感知-动作耦合。这一问题在类人机器人球拍类运动中尤为突出：成功的击球依赖于精确的视觉跟踪、轨迹预测、协调步伐以及稳定的全身击打控制。现有机器人球拍运动系统通常依赖外部动作捕捉进行状态估计，或依赖特定任务的底层控制器，而这些控制器往往需要在不同任务和平台之间反复重新训练。我们提出 CyboRacket，一种面向类人球拍运动的分层“感知到动作”框架，将机载视觉感知、基于物理的轨迹预测以及大规模预训练的全身控制相结合。该框架利用机载相机跟踪来球，预测其未来轨迹，并将估计得到的拦截状态转化为末端执行器与底盘运动的目标指令，进而由 Unitree G1 类人机器人上的 SONIC 控制器完成全身执行。我们在基于视觉的类人网球击球任务中对该框架进行了评估。实验结果表明，在完全依赖机载传感的情况下，系统能够实现实时视觉跟踪、轨迹预测以及成功击球。
Dynamic ball-interaction tasks remain challenging for robots because they require tight perception-action coupling under limited reaction time. This challenge is especially pronounced in humanoid racket sports, where successful interception depends on accurate visual tracking, trajectory prediction, coordinated stepping, and stable whole-body striking. Existing robotic racket-sport systems often rely on external motion capture for state estimation or on task-specific low-level controllers that must be retrained across tasks and platforms. We present CyboRacket, a hierarchical perception-to-action framework for humanoid racket sports that integrates onboard visual perception, physics-based trajectory prediction, and large-scale pre-trained whole-body control. The framework uses onboard cameras to track the incoming object, predicts its future trajectory, and converts the estimated interception state into target end-effector and base-motion commands for whole-body execution by SONIC on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. We evaluate the proposed framework in a vision-based humanoid tennis-hitting task. Experimental results demonstrate real-time visual tracking, trajectory prediction, and successful striking using purely onboard sensing.
Pro-HOI: Perceptive Root-guided Humanoid-Object Interaction
Pro-HOI：感知根引导的人形-物体交互
类人机器人执行可靠的物体交互（Humanoid-Object Interaction, HOI）任务，常受到通用控制接口缺乏和闭环感知机制不稳健的制约。本文提出了 Pro-HOI（Perceptive Root-guided Humanoid-Object Interaction），一个面向稳健类人机器人运动操作的可推广框架。首先，我们收集适用于真实部署的搬运箱子动作，并通过符号距离场（Signed Distance Field）损失优化穿透伪影。其次，我们提出了一种新型训练框架：策略以期望的根部轨迹为条件，仅将参考动作作为奖励信号使用。这一设计不仅消除了复杂奖励调优的需求，还将根部轨迹建立为高层规划器的通用接口，使导航与运动操作能够同时进行。此外，为确保操作可靠性，我们引入了持久化物体估计模块，通过实时检测与数字孪生融合，使机器人能够自主检测物体滑动并触发重新抓取动作。在 Unitree G1 机器人上的实证验证表明，Pro-HOI 在泛化能力和鲁棒性方面显著优于基线方法，并能在复杂真实环境中实现长期可靠的任务执行。
Executing reliable Humanoid-Object Interaction (HOI) tasks for humanoid robots is hindered by the lack of generalized control interfaces and robust closed-loop perception mechanisms. In this work, we introduce Perceptive Root-guided Humanoid-Object Interaction, Pro-HOI, a generalizable framework for robust humanoid loco-manipulation. First, we collect box-carrying motions that are suitable for real-world deployment and optimize penetration artifacts through a Signed Distance Field loss. Second, we propose a novel training framework that conditions the policy on a desired root-trajectory while utilizing reference motion exclusively as a reward. This design not only eliminates the need for intricate reward tuning but also establishes root trajectory as a universal interface for high-level planners, enabling simultaneous navigation and loco-manipulation. Furthermore, to ensure operational reliability, we incorporate a persistent object estimation module. By fusing real-time detection with Digital Twin, this module allows the robot to autonomously detect slippage and trigger re-grasping maneuvers. Empirical validation on a Unitree G1 robot demonstrates that Pro-HOI significantly outperforms baselines in generalization and robustness, achieving reliable long-horizon execution in complex real-world scenarios.
ZeroWBC: Learning Natural Visuomotor Humanoid Control Directly from Human Egocentric Video
ZeroWBC：直接从人类自我中心视频中学习自然视觉运动人形控制
实现类人机器人对场景的多样化自然全身控制仍是重大挑战。尽管一些近期研究展示了自主类人交互控制，但它们通常受限于固定步态模式或昂贵的遥操作数据收集，缺乏执行更自然人类行为（如坐下或踢球）的灵活性。此外，获取真实机器人遥操作数据成本高昂且耗时。为解决这些问题，我们提出 ZeroWBC，一种全新框架，可直接从人类自中心视频中学习自然的类人视觉-运动控制策略，无需大规模机器人遥操作数据，从而实现自然的类人机器人场景交互控制。具体而言，我们的方法首先微调视觉-语言模型（VLM），根据文本指令和自中心视觉上下文预测未来全身人类动作，然后将生成的动作重定向到真实机器人关节，并通过稳健的通用运动跟踪策略实现类人全身控制。在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上的大量实验表明，该方法在动作自然性和多样性方面均优于基线方法，成功建立了一条无需遥操作数据收集的全身控制管线，为通用类人全身控制提供了可扩展且高效的范式。
Achieving versatile and naturalistic whole-body control for humanoid robot scene-interaction remains a significant challenge. While some recent works have demonstrated autonomous humanoid interactive control, they are constrained to rigid locomotion patterns and expensive teleoperation data collection, lacking the versatility to execute more human-like natural behaviors such as sitting or kicking. Furthermore, acquiring the necessary real robot teleoperation data is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming. To address these limitations, we introduce ZeroWBC, a novel framework that learns a natural humanoid visuomotor control policy directly from human egocentric videos, eliminating the need for large-scale robot teleoperation data and enabling natural humanoid robot scene-interaction control. Specifically, our approach first fine-tunes a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to predict future whole-body human motions based on text instructions and egocentric visual context, then these generated motions are retargeted to real robot joints and executed via our robust general motion tracking policy for humanoid whole-body control. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline approaches in motion naturalness and versatility, successfully establishing a pipeline that eliminates teleoperation data collection overhead for whole-body humanoid control, offering a scalable and efficient paradigm for general humanoid whole-body control.
Learning Athletic Humanoid Tennis Skills from Imperfect Human Motion Data
从不完美的人体运动数据中学习类人机器人的网球运动技能
人类运动员能够展现出多样且高度动态的网球技能，从而与高速来球进行高水平对抗回合。然而，在类人机器人上复现此类行为极具挑战，其中一个重要原因是缺乏高质量的类人动作数据或网球场景中的完整人体运动学数据作为参考。为此，我们提出 LATENT（从不完美人类运动数据中学习类人网球技能的系统）。这些不完美的人类数据仅包含在网球运动中使用的基本技能片段，而非真实比赛中的完整精确动作序列，从而显著降低了数据采集难度。我们的核心洞见在于，尽管数据不完美，这类近似真实的数据仍然蕴含了网球场景下人类基本技能的先验信息。通过进一步的校正与组合，我们学习得到一种类人策略，使机器人能够在多种条件下稳定击打来球并将其回击至目标位置，同时保持自然的动作风格。我们还提出了一系列增强仿真到现实迁移鲁棒性的设计，并将该策略部署在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上。实验结果表明，该方法在真实环境中取得了令人瞩目的表现，能够与人类玩家稳定地进行多拍对打。
Human athletes demonstrate versatile and highly-dynamic tennis skills to successfully conduct competitive rallies with a high-speed tennis ball. However, reproducing such behaviors on humanoid robots is difficult, partially due to the lack of perfect humanoid action data or human kinematic motion data in tennis scenarios as reference. In this work, we propose LATENT, a system that Learns Athletic humanoid TEnnis skills from imperfect human motioN daTa. The imperfect human motion data consist only of motion fragments that capture the primitive skills used when playing tennis rather than precise and complete human-tennis motion sequences from real-world tennis matches, thereby significantly reducing the difficulty of data collection. Our key insight is that, despite being imperfect, such quasi-realistic data still provide priors about human primitive skills in tennis scenarios. With further correction and composition, we learn a humanoid policy that can consistently strike incoming balls under a wide range of conditions and return them to target locations, while preserving natural motion styles. We also propose a series of designs for robust sim-to-real transfer and deploy our policy on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. Our method achieves surprising results in the real world and can stably sustain multi-shot rallies with human players.
PhysMoDPO: Physically-Plausible Humanoid Motion with Preference Optimization
PhysMoDPO：基于偏好优化的物理上合理的类人运动
近年来，文本条件的人体动作生成取得了显著进展，这主要得益于在大规模人体运动数据上训练的扩散模型。在此基础上，最新方法尝试通过引入全身控制器（WBC），将扩散模型生成的动作转换为可执行轨迹，从而应用于角色动画与真实机器人控制。然而，尽管 WBC 可使轨迹符合物理约束，其结果往往与原始动作存在显著偏差。为解决这一问题，我们提出 PhysMoDPO，一种基于直接偏好优化（Direct Preference Optimization）的框架。不同于依赖脚滑惩罚等手工设计物理启发式的方法，我们将 WBC 融入训练流程中，直接优化扩散模型，使其在经过 WBC 后的输出既满足物理一致性，又符合原始文本指令。为训练 PhysMoDPO，我们引入基于物理和任务的奖励函数，对生成轨迹进行偏好排序并据此优化模型。在文本到动作生成与空间控制任务上的大量实验表明，PhysMoDPO 在物理真实感和任务性能指标上均实现了稳定提升。此外，我们还展示了该方法在仿真中的零样本动作迁移以及在真实 Unitree G1 类人机器人部署中的显著性能改进。
Recent progress in text-conditioned human motion generation has been largely driven by diffusion models trained on large-scale human motion data. Building on this progress, recent methods attempt to transfer such models for character animation and real robot control by applying a Whole-Body Controller (WBC) that converts diffusion-generated motions into executable trajectories. While WBC trajectories become compliant with physics, they may expose substantial deviations from original motion. To address this issue, we here propose PhysMoDPO, a Direct Preference Optimization framework. Unlike prior work that relies on hand-crafted physics-aware heuristics such as foot-sliding penalties, we integrate WBC into our training pipeline and optimize diffusion model such that the output of WBC becomes compliant both with physics and original text instructions. To train PhysMoDPO we deploy physics-based and task-specific rewards and use them to assign preference to synthesized trajectories. Our extensive experiments on text-to-motion and spatial control tasks demonstrate consistent improvements of PhysMoDPO in both physical realism and task-related metrics on simulated robots. Moreover, we demonstrate that PhysMoDPO results in significant improvements when applied to zero-shot motion transfer in simulation and for real-world deployment on a G1 humanoid robot.
CMoE: Contrastive Mixture of Experts for Motion Control and Terrain Adaptation of Humanoid Robots
CMoE：用于人形机器人运动控制和地形适应的对比专家混合模型
为了在真实环境中有效部署，人形机器人必须能够自主地在各种复杂地形（包括突变地形）中导航。虽然传统的专家混合模型（MoE）框架理论上能够对各种地形特征进行建模，但实际上，其门控网络在不同地形上表现出几乎一致的专家激活值，削弱了专家的专业化程度，限制了模型的表达能力。为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了CMoE，一种新型的单阶段强化学习框架，它融合了对比学习来优化专家激活分布。通过施加对比约束，CMoE最大化了同一地形内专家激活值的一致性，同时最小化了不同地形间的相似性，从而鼓励专家专注于不同的地形类型。我们通过一系列具有挑战性的实验，在Unitree G1人形机器人上验证了我们的方法。结果表明，CMoE使机器人能够跨越高达20厘米的连续台阶和宽达80厘米的间隙，并在各种混合地形上实现稳健自然的步态，超越了现有方法的局限性。为了支持进一步的研究和促进社区发展，我们将代码公开发布。
For effective deployment in real-world environments, humanoid robots must autonomously navigate a diverse range of complex terrains with abrupt transitions. While the Vanilla mixture of experts (MoE) framework is theoretically capable of modeling diverse terrain features, in practice, the gating network exhibits nearly uniform expert activations across different terrains, weakening the expert specialization and limiting the model's expressive power. To address this limitation, we introduce CMoE, a novel single-stage reinforcement learning framework that integrates contrastive learning to refine expert activation distributions. By imposing contrastive constraints, CMoE maximizes the consistency of expert activations within the same terrain while minimizing their similarity across different terrains, thereby encouraging experts to specialize in distinct terrain types. We validated our approach on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot through a series of challenging experiments. Results demonstrate that CMoE enables the robot to traverse continuous steps up to 20 cm high and gaps up to 80 cm wide, while achieving robust and natural gait across diverse mixed terrains, surpassing the limits of existing methods. To support further research and foster community development, we release our code publicly.
DiT4DiT: Jointly Modeling Video Dynamics and Actions for Generalizable Robot Control
DiT4DiT：联合建模视频动力学和动作以实现通用机器人控制
视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型已成为机器人学习领域一个极具前景的范式，但其表征仍然主要继承自静态图像-文本预训练，导致物理动力学只能从相对有限的动作数据中学习。相比之下，生成式视频模型编码了丰富的时空结构和隐式物理信息，使其成为机器人操作的理想基础。然而，其潜力尚未在文献中得到充分挖掘。为了弥补这一差距，我们提出了DiT4DiT，一个端到端的视频-动作模型，它将视频扩散变换器（Diffusion Transformer）与动作扩散变换器（Diffusion Transformer）耦合在一个统一的级联框架中。DiT4DiT并非依赖于重建的未来帧，而是从视频生成过程中提取中间去噪特征，并将其作为动作预测的时间基础条件。此外，我们还提出了一种双流匹配目标函数，该函数对视频预测、隐藏状态提取和动作推理分别采用解耦的时间步长和噪声尺度，从而实现了两个模块的协同训练。在仿真和实际基准测试中，DiT4DiT 均取得了最先进的成果，在 LIBERO 和 RoboCasa GR1 上分别达到了平均 98.6% 和 50.8% 的成功率，且使用的训练数据量显著减少。在 Unitree G1 机器人上，它也展现出了卓越的实际性能和强大的零样本泛化能力。更重要的是，DiT4DiT 将样本效率提高了 10 倍以上，并将收敛速度提高了 7 倍，这表明视频生成可以作为机器人策略学习的有效扩展代理。
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot learning, but their representations are still largely inherited from static image-text pretraining, leaving physical dynamics to be learned from comparatively limited action data. Generative video models, by contrast, encode rich spatiotemporal structure and implicit physics, making them a compelling foundation for robotic manipulation. But their potentials are not fully explored in the literature. To bridge the gap, we introduce DiT4DiT, an end-to-end Video-Action Model that couples a video Diffusion Transformer with an action Diffusion Transformer in a unified cascaded framework. Instead of relying on reconstructed future frames, DiT4DiT extracts intermediate denoising features from the video generation process and uses them as temporally grounded conditions for action prediction. We further propose a dual flow-matching objective with decoupled timesteps and noise scales for video prediction, hidden-state extraction, and action inference, enabling coherent joint training of both modules. Across simulation and real-world benchmarks, DiT4DiT achieves state-of-the-art results, reaching average success rates of 98.6% on LIBERO and 50.8% on RoboCasa GR1 while using substantially less training data. On the Unitree G1 robot, it also delivers superior real-world performance and strong zero-shot generalization. Importantly, DiT4DiT improves sample efficiency by over 10x and speeds up convergence by up to 7x, demonstrating that video generation can serve as an effective scaling proxy for robot policy learning.
Coordinated Humanoid Robot Locomotion with Symmetry Equivariant Reinforcement Learning Policy
基于对称等变强化学习策略的协调人形机器人运动
人类神经系统具有双侧对称性，使其能够协调平衡地运动。然而，现有的人形机器人深度强化学习（DRL）方法忽略了机器人的形态对称性，导致其行为不协调且性能欠佳。受人类运动控制的启发，我们提出了对称等变策略（SE-Policy），这是一种新的DRL框架，它在执行器（Actor）中嵌入了严格的对称等变性，在评判器（Criticer）中嵌入了对称不变性，且无需额外的超参数。SE-Policy能够确保对称观测结果的一致性，从而产生时空协调的运动，并提升任务性能。我们使用Unitree G1人形机器人，在仿真和实际部署环境中进行了大量的速度跟踪任务实验。结果表明，与最先进的基线方法相比，SE-Policy在实现更优时空协调性的同时，将跟踪精度提高了高达40%。这些结果证明了SE-Policy的有效性及其在人形机器人领域的广泛适用性。
The human nervous system exhibits bilateral symmetry, enabling coordinated and balanced movements. However, existing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods for humanoid robots neglect morphological symmetry of the robot, leading to uncoordinated and suboptimal behaviors. Inspired by human motor control, we propose Symmetry Equivariant Policy (SE-Policy), a new DRL framework that embeds strict symmetry equivariance in the actor and symmetry invariance in the critic without additional hyperparameters. SE-Policy enforces consistent behaviors across symmetric observations, producing temporally and spatially coordinated motions with higher task performance. Extensive experiments on velocity tracking tasks, conducted in both simulation and real-world deployment with the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, demonstrate that SE-Policy improves tracking accuracy by up to 40% compared to state-of-the-art baselines, while achieving superior spatial-temporal coordination. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SE-Policy and its broad applicability to humanoid robots.
OmniDP: Beyond-FOV Large-Workspace Humanoid Manipulation with Omnidirectional 3D Perception
OmniDP：超越视场角的大型工作空间人形机器人操控，具备全方位3D感知能力

The deployment of humanoid robots for dexterous manipulation in unstructured environments remains challenging due to perceptual limitations that constrain the effective workspace. In scenarios where physical constraints prevent the robot from repositioning itself, maintaining omnidirectional awareness becomes far more critical than color or semantic this http URL recent advances in visuomotor policy learning have improved manipulation capabilities, conventional RGB-D solutions suffer from narrow fields of view (FOV) and self-occlusion, requiring frequent base movements that introduce motion uncertainty and safety risks. Existing approaches to expanding perception, including active vision systems and third-view cameras, introduce mechanical complexity, calibration dependencies, and latency that hinder reliable real-time performance.
