Make Tracking Easy: Neural Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Whole-body Control
让追踪变得轻松：用于人形机器人全身控制的神经运动重定向
人形机器人需要多种运动技能才能融入复杂的环境，但如何弥合人类数据在运动学和动力学方面的差距仍然是一个主要瓶颈。我们通过 Hessian 分析证明，传统的基于优化的重定向方法本质上是非凸的，容易陷入局部最优解，从而导致关节跳跃和自身穿透等物理伪影。为了解决这个问题，我们将目标定位问题重新表述为学习数据分布，而不是优化最优解，并提出了 NMR，一个神经运动重定向框架，它将静态几何映射转换为动态感知的学习过程。我们首先提出了聚类专家物理精细化 (CEPR)，这是一个分层数据管道，它利用基于变分自编码器 (VAE) 的运动聚类将异构运动分组为潜在模式。该策略显著降低了大规模并行强化学习专家的计算开销，这些专家负责将带有噪声的人类演示投影并修复到机器人的可行运动流形上。由此产生的高保真数据用于监督非自回归 CNN-Transformer 架构，该架构基于全局时间上下文进行推理，以抑制重建噪声并绕过几何陷阱。在 Unitree G1 人形机器人上进行的实验涵盖了多种动态任务（例如武术、舞蹈），结果表明，与最先进的基线方法相比，NMR 能够消除关节跳跃并显著减少自身碰撞。此外，NMR 生成的参考数据能够加速下游全身控制策略的收敛，从而为弥合人机具身认知差距提供了一条可扩展的途径。
Humanoid robots require diverse motor skills to integrate into complex environments, but bridging the kinematic and dynamic embodiment gap from human data remains a major bottleneck. We demonstrate through Hessian analysis that traditional optimization-based retargeting is inherently non-convex and prone to local optima, leading to physical artifacts like joint jumps and self-penetration. To address this, we reformulate the targeting problem as learning data distribution rather than optimizing optimal solutions, where we propose NMR, a Neural Motion Retargeting framework that transforms static geometric mapping into a dynamics-aware learned process. We first propose Clustered-Expert Physics Refinement (CEPR), a hierarchical data pipeline that leverages VAE-based motion clustering to group heterogeneous movements into latent motifs. This strategy significantly reduces the computational overhead of massively parallel reinforcement learning experts, which project and repair noisy human demonstrations onto the robot's feasible motion manifold. The resulting high-fidelity data supervises a non-autoregressive CNN-Transformer architecture that reasons over global temporal context to suppress reconstruction noise and bypass geometric traps. Experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid across diverse dynamic tasks (e.g., martial arts, dancing) show that NMR eliminates joint jumps and significantly reduces self-collisions compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Furthermore, NMR-generated references accelerate the convergence of downstream whole-body control policies, establishing a scalable path for bridging the human-robot embodiment gap.
Active Stereo-Camera Outperforms Multi-Sensor Setup in ACT Imitation Learning for Humanoid Manipulation
在用于人形机器人操作的ACT模仿学习中，主动式立体相机优于多传感器设置
教导类人机器人新任务的复杂性是阻碍其在工业领域广泛应用的主要原因之一。尽管模仿学习（IL），尤其是基于Transformer的动作分块技术（ACT），能够使机器人快速习得任务，但在执行操作任务所需的最佳传感硬件方面尚未达成共识。本文在配备三指手的Unitree G1类人机器人上，针对两类操作任务对14种传感器组合进行了基准测试。我们明确评估了触觉、本体感受与主动视觉模态的集成效果。分析表明，在数据受限的情况下，策略性的传感器选择可以在减少计算开销的同时，性能优于复杂的配置方案。我们开发了一个开源的统一消融框架，通过对综合主数据集进行传感器掩蔽处理来开展研究。结果表明，在有限数据的模仿学习中，增加额外的模态往往会降低性能。一套极简的主动双目相机配置在空间泛化任务中实现了87.5%的成功率，在结构化操作任务中达到了94.4%，表现优于复杂的多传感器配置。相反，由于信噪比低，在上述配置中增加压力传感器反而使后一任务的成功率降至67.3%。我们得出结论，在数据有限的情况下，主动视觉在鲁棒性与复杂性之间提供了更优的权衡。尽管触觉模态可能需要更大的数据集才能发挥作用，但我们的研究证实，策略性的传感器选择对于设计高效的学习过程至关重要。
The complexity of teaching humanoid robots new tasks is one of the major reasons hindering their widespread adoption in the industry. While Imitation Learning (IL), particularly Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), enables rapid task acquisition, there is no consensus yet on the optimal sensory hardware required for manipulation tasks. This paper benchmarks 14 sensor combinations on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot equipped with three-finger hands for two manipulation tasks. We explicitly evaluate the integration of tactile and proprioceptive modalities alongside active vision. Our analysis demonstrates that strategic sensor selection can outperform complex configurations in data-limited regimes while reducing computational overhead. We develop an open-source Unified Ablation Framework that utilizes sensor masking on a comprehensive master dataset. Results indicate that additional modalities often degrade performance for IL with limited data. A minimal active stereo-camera setup outperformed complex multi-sensor configurations, achieving 87.5% success in a spatial generalization task and 94.4% in a structured manipulation task. Conversely, adding pressure sensors to this setup reduced success to 67.3% in the latter task due to a low signal-to-noise ratio. We conclude that in data-limited regimes, active vision offers a superior trade-off between robustness and complexity. While tactile modalities may require larger datasets to be effective, our findings validate that strategic sensor selection is critical for designing an efficient learning process.
Chasing Autonomy: Dynamic Retargeting and Control Guided RL for Performant and Controllable Humanoid Running
追求自主性：动态重定向和控制引导强化学习实现高性能、可控的人形机器人跑步
类人机器人有望像人类一样运动，包括快速且富有爆发力的奔跑。近期，能够模拟人类动作的强化学习（RL）控制器因其能生成极具动态性的行为而备受关注，但这类控制器往往局限于单一动作的回放，从而阻碍了其在长时自主运动中的部署。在本文中，我们提出了一套流水线，通过带有硬约束的优化程序对人类动作进行动态重定向，从而由单次人类演示生成改进的周期性参考运动库。随后，我们研究了参考动作和奖励结构对参考速度及指令速度跟踪的影响，得出结论：在跟踪动态优化后的人类数据时，采用目标条件化且控制引导的奖励机制能获得最佳性能。我们将该策略部署于硬件，在Unitree G1机器人上实现了高达3.3 m/s的奔跑速度，并在真实环境中完成了数百公里的持续行走，验证了其速度与耐力。此外，为展示该运动控制的可控性，我们将控制器集成到包含感知与规划的全自主堆栈中，实现了室外奔跑过程中的避障。
Humanoid robots have the promise of locomoting like humans, including fast and dynamic running. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) controllers that can mimic human motions have become popular as they can generate very dynamic behaviors, but they are often restricted to single motion play-back which hinders their deployment in long duration and autonomous locomotion. In this paper, we present a pipeline to dynamically retarget human motions through an optimization routine with hard constraints to generate improved periodic reference libraries from a single human demonstration. We then study the effect of both the reference motion and the reward structure on the reference and commanded velocity tracking, concluding that a goal-conditioned and control-guided reward which tracks dynamically optimized human data results in the best performance. We deploy the policy on hardware, demonstrating its speed and endurance by achieving running speeds of up to 3.3 m/s on a Unitree G1 robot and traversing hundreds of meters in real-world environments. Additionally, to demonstrate the controllability of the locomotion, we use the controller in a full perception and planning autonomy stack for obstacle avoidance while running outdoors.
Learning Humanoid Navigation from Human Data
从人类数据中学习人形机器人导航
我们提出 EgoNav 系统，该系统使类人机器人能够仅通过学习 5 小时的人类行走数据，在完全没有机器人数据或微调的情况下，遍历各种陌生的环境。扩散模型根据过去轨迹、融合颜色、深度与语义的 360° 视觉记忆，以及来自冻结 DINOv3 主干网络、可捕捉深度传感器无法识别的外观线索的视频特征，来预测可能的未来轨迹分布。一种混合采样方案通过 10 个去噪步骤实现实时推理，并由收缩时域控制器从预测分布中选择路径。我们通过离线评估验证了 EgoNav，其在避障和多模态覆盖方面优于基准模型；同时，我们在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上进行了跨室内外未知环境的零样本部署。诸如等待门开、绕过人群以及避开玻璃墙等行为，均从习得的先验知识中自然涌现。我们将开源该数据集和预训练模型。
We present EgoNav, a system that enables a humanoid robot to traverse diverse, unseen environments by learning entirely from 5 hours of human walking data, with no robot data or finetuning. A diffusion model predicts distributions of plausible future trajectories conditioned on past trajectory, a 360 deg visual memory fusing color, depth, and semantics, and video features from a frozen DINOv3 backbone that capture appearance cues invisible to depth sensors. A hybrid sampling scheme achieves real-time inference in 10 denoising steps, and a receding-horizon controller selects paths from the predicted distribution. We validate EgoNav through offline evaluations, where it outperforms baselines in collision avoidance and multi-modal coverage, and through zero-shot deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid across unseen indoor and outdoor environments. Behaviors such as waiting for doors to open, navigating around crowds, and avoiding glass walls emerge naturally from the learned prior. We will release the dataset and trained models.
PhysiFlow: Physics-Aware Humanoid Whole-Body VLA via Multi-Brain Latent Flow Matching and Robust Tracking
PhysiFlow：基于多脑潜在流匹配和鲁棒跟踪的物理感知人形全身VLA
在类人机器人控制领域，视觉-语言-动作（VLA）与全身控制的融合对于语义引导下的现实世界任务执行至关重要。然而，现有方法面临着 VLA 推理效率低，或全身控制缺乏有效语义引导的挑战，导致肢体协调的动态任务出现不稳定。为了填补这一空白，我们提出了一种语义-运动意图引导、物理感知的多脑 VLA 类人机器人全身控制框架。我们通过一系列实验评估了该框架的性能。实验结果表明，该框架使 Unitree G1 类人机器人能够实现可靠的视觉语言引导下的全身协同。
In the domain of humanoid robot control, the fusion of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) with whole-body control is essential for semantically guided execution of real-world tasks. However, existing methods encounter challenges in terms of low VLA inference efficiency or an absence of effective semantic guidance for whole-body control, resulting in instability in dynamic limb-coordinated tasks. To bridge this gap, we present a semantic-motion intent guided, physics-aware multi-brain VLA framework for humanoid whole-body control. A series of experiments was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed framework. The experimental results demonstrated that the framework enabled reliable vision-language-guided full-body coordination for Unitree G1 humanoid robots.
DreamControl-v2: Simpler and Scalable Autonomous Humanoid Skills via Trainable Guided Diffusion Priors
DreamControl-v2：通过可训练的引导扩散先验实现更简单、可扩展的自主人形机器人技能
为类人机器人开发鲁棒的自主移动操作（loco-manipulation）技能仍是机器人领域一个悬而未决的问题。虽然强化学习（RL）已成功应用于足式行走，但由于操作任务面临长时程规划的挑战，将其应用于复杂的、充满交互的操作任务则更为困难。针对这一问题，近期出现了一种名为 DreamControl 的方法，它利用现成的人类运动扩散模型作为生成先验，在训练期间引导 RL 策略。在本文中，我们研究了 DreamControl 运动先验的影响，并提出了一种改进框架，该框架直接在类人机器人的运动空间内训练引导扩散模型，将多样化的人类与机器人数据集聚合到一个统一的具身空间中。我们证明，由于采用了更大规模的训练数据混合，我们的方法能够捕捉到更广泛的技能，并通过消除人工过滤干预建立了更加自动化的流程。此外，我们表明，扩展参考轨迹的生成对于获得鲁棒的下游 RL 策略至关重要。我们通过在仿真环境及真实 Unitree-G1 机器人上的广泛实验验证了我们的方法。
Developing robust autonomous loco-manipulation skills for humanoids remains an open problem in robotics. While RL has been applied successfully to legged locomotion, applying it to complex, interaction-rich manipulation tasks is harder given long-horizon planning challenges for manipulation. A recent approach along these lines is DreamControl, which addresses these issues by leveraging off-the-shelf human motion diffusion models as a generative prior to guide RL policies during training. In this paper, we investigate the impact of DreamControl's motion prior and propose an improved framework that trains a guided diffusion model directly in the humanoid robot's motion space, aggregating diverse human and robot datasets into a unified embodiment space. We demonstrate that our approach captures a wider range of skills due to the larger training data mixture and establishes a more automated pipeline by removing the need for manual filtering interventions. Furthermore, we show that scaling the generation of reference trajectories is important for achieving robust downstream RL policies. We validate our approach through extensive experiments in simulation and on a real Unitree-G1.
Towards Adaptive Humanoid Control via Multi-Behavior Distillation and Reinforced Fine-Tuning
通过多行为提炼和强化微调实现自适应人形机器人控制
类人机器人有望学习多种类似人类的运动行为，包括站立、行走、跑步和跳跃。然而，现有方法主要要求为每项技能训练独立策略，导致生成的行为特定控制器在部署于不规则地形和多样化场景时，表现出泛化性受限且性能脆弱。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了自适应类人控制（AHC），该方案采用两阶段框架来学习跨不同技能和地形的自适应类人运动控制器。具体而言，我们首先训练数个基础运动策略，并执行多行为蒸馏过程以获取基础多行为控制器，从而实现基于环境的自适应行为切换。随后，我们通过收集在更多样化地形上执行自适应行为时的在线反馈来进行强化微调，增强控制器的地形适应性。我们在仿真环境和 Unitree G1 机器人真实场景中均进行了实验。结果表明，我们的方法在各种情况和地形下均表现出极强的适应性。
Humanoid robots are promising to learn a diverse set of human-like locomotion behaviors, including standing up, walking, running, and jumping. However, existing methods predominantly require training independent policies for each skill, yielding behavior-specific controllers that exhibit limited generalization and brittle performance when deployed on irregular terrains and in diverse situations. To address this challenge, we propose Adaptive Humanoid Control (AHC) that adopts a two-stage framework to learn an adaptive humanoid locomotion controller across different skills and terrains. Specifically, we first train several primary locomotion policies and perform a multi-behavior distillation process to obtain a basic multi-behavior controller, facilitating adaptive behavior switching based on the environment. Then, we perform reinforced fine-tuning by collecting online feedback in performing adaptive behaviors on more diverse terrains, enhancing terrain adaptability for the controller. We conduct experiments in both simulation and real-world experiments in Unitree G1 robots. The results show that our method exhibits strong adaptability across various situations and terrains.
BAT: Balancing Agility and Stability via Online Policy Switching for Long-Horizon Whole-Body Humanoid Control
BAT：通过在线策略切换平衡敏捷性和稳定性，实现长时程全身人形机器人控制
尽管在控制、强化学习和模仿学习领域取得了近期进展，但开发一个能够实现敏捷、精确且鲁棒的全身行为（尤其是在长时程任务中）的统一框架仍然具有挑战性。现有方法通常遵循两种范式：用于全局协作的耦合全身策略和用于模块化精度的解耦策略。然而，如果缺乏系统性的集成方法，敏捷性、鲁棒性与精度之间的权衡仍难以解决。在这项工作中，我们提出了 BAT，这是一个在线策略切换框架，通过在两个互补的全身强化学习控制器之间进行动态选择，以平衡不同运动语境下的敏捷性与稳定性。我们的框架由两个互补模块组成：一个通过分层强化学习并结合滑动时界策略预评估专家引导所习得的切换策略，以及一个通过离散运动序列预测选项偏好以增强泛化性能的选项感知 VQ-VAE。最终决策通过两个模块的置信度加权融合获得。在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上进行的大量仿真和真实世界实验表明，BAT 能够实现多功能的长时程移动操作，并在多种任务中优于以往的方法。
Despite recent advances in control, reinforcement learning, and imitation learning, developing a unified framework that can achieve agile, precise, and robust whole-body behaviors, particularly in long-horizon tasks, remains challenging. Existing approaches typically follow two paradigms: coupled whole-body policies for global coordination and decoupled policies for modular precision. However, without a systematic method to integrate both, this trade-off between agility, robustness, and precision remains unresolved. In this work, we propose BAT, an online policy-switching framework that dynamically selects between two complementary whole-body RL controllers to balance agility and stability across different motion contexts. Our framework consists of two complementary modules: a switching policy learned via hierarchical RL with an expert guidance from sliding-horizon policy pre-evaluation, and an option-aware VQ-VAE that predicts option preference from discrete motion token sequences for improved generalization. The final decision is obtained via confidence-weighted fusion of two modules. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments on the Unitree G1 humanoid robot demonstrate that BAT enables versatile long-horizon loco-manipulation and outperforms prior methods across diverse tasks.
InterReal: A Unified Physics-Based Imitation Framework for Learning Human-Object Interaction Skills
InterReal：一个基于统一物理原理的模仿框架，用于学习人机交互技能
交互是类人机器人的核心能力之一。然而，现有的大多数框架都集中在非交互式的全身控制上，这限制了它们的实际应用性。在这项工作中，我们开发了 InterReal，这是一个统一的基于物理的模仿学习框架，用于现实世界中的人机交互（HOI）控制。InterReal 使类人机器人能够跟踪 HOI 参考运动，从而促进了精细交互技能的学习及其在现实环境中的部署。在该框架内，我们首先引入了一种带有手部-物体接触约束的 HOI 运动数据增强方案，并利用增强后的运动来提高策略在物体扰动下的稳定性。其次，我们提出了一种自动奖励学习器，以解决大规模奖励塑形的挑战。由关键跟踪误差指标引导的元策略负责探索奖励信号，并将其分配给底层强化学习目标，从而实现了更有效的交互策略学习。针对搬箱和推箱 HOI 任务的实验表明，与近期基准方法相比，InterReal 实现了最佳的跟踪精度和最高的任务成功率。此外，我们在真实机器人 Unitree G1 上验证了该框架，证明了其在仿真之外的实际有效性和鲁棒性。
Interaction is one of the core abilities of humanoid robots. However, most existing frameworks focus on non-interactive whole-body control, which limits their practical applicability. In this work, we develop InterReal, a unified physics-based imitation learning framework for Real-world human-object Interaction (HOI) control. InterReal enables humanoid robots to track HOI reference motions, facilitating the learning of fine-grained interactive skills and their deployment in real-world settings. Within this framework, we first introduce a HOI motion data augmentation scheme with hand-object contact constraints, and utilize the augmented motions to improve policy stability under object perturbations. Second, we propose an automatic reward learner to address the challenge of large-scale reward shaping. A meta-policy guided by critical tracking error metrics explores and allocates reward signals to the low-level reinforcement learning objective, which enables more effective learning of interactive policies. Experiments on HOI tasks of box-picking and box-pushing demonstrate that InterReal achieves the best tracking accuracy and the highest task success rate compared to recent baselines. Furthermore, we validate the framework on the real-world robot Unitree G1, which demonstrates its practical effectiveness and robustness beyond simulation.
ECHO: Edge-Cloud Humanoid Orchestration for Language-to-Motion Control
ECHO：用于语言到动作控制的边缘云人形机器人编排
我们提出 ECHO，一个用于类人机器人语言驱动全身控制的边云协同框架。云端部署的基于扩散模型的文本生成运动（text-to-motion）生成器负责从自然语言指令合成参考运动，而边缘侧部署的强化学习跟踪器则在机器人上以闭环方式执行这些运动。这两个模块通过一个紧凑的、机器人原生的 38 维运动表示进行衔接，该表示编码了每帧的关节角度、根部平面速度、根部高度以及连续的 6D 根部朝向，消除了推理阶段从人体模型进行重定向的需求，并与底层 PD 控制直接兼容。生成器采用一维卷积 UNet 架构，并使用 CLIP 编码的文本特征进行交叉注意力调节；在推理时，通过 10 个去噪步骤的 DDIM 采样和无分类器引导，在云端 GPU 上仅需约一秒即可生成运动序列。跟踪器遵循“教师-学生”范式：将特权教师策略蒸馏给配备证据自适应模块的轻量化学生策略以实现从仿真到现实的迁移，并通过形态对称性约束和领域随机化进一步增强。自主跌倒恢复机制通过车载 IMU 读数检测跌倒，并从预构建的运动库中检索恢复轨迹。我们在重定向后的 HumanML3D 基准上对 ECHO 进行了评估，在统一的机器人域评估器下，它实现了极高的生成质量（FID 0.029，R-Precision Top-1 0.686），同时保持了高度的运动安全性和轨迹一致性。在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上进行的真实世界实验证明，该框架在无需任何硬件微调的情况下，即可稳定执行多样的文本指令。
We present ECHO, an edge--cloud framework for language-driven whole-body control of humanoid robots. A cloud-hosted diffusion-based text-to-motion generator synthesizes motion references from natural language instructions, while an edge-deployed reinforcement-learning tracker executes them in closed loop on the robot. The two modules are bridged by a compact, robot-native 38-dimensional motion representation that encodes joint angles, root planar velocity, root height, and a continuous 6D root orientation per frame, eliminating inference-time retargeting from human body models and remaining directly compatible with low-level PD control. The generator adopts a 1D convolutional UNet with cross-attention conditioned on CLIP-encoded text features; at inference, DDIM sampling with 10 denoising steps and classifier-free guidance produces motion sequences in approximately one second on a cloud GPU. The tracker follows a Teacher--Student paradigm: a privileged teacher policy is distilled into a lightweight student equipped with an evidential adaptation module for sim-to-real transfer, further strengthened by morphological symmetry constraints and domain randomization. An autonomous fall recovery mechanism detects falls via onboard IMU readings and retrieves recovery trajectories from a pre-built motion library. We evaluate ECHO on a retargeted HumanML3D benchmark, where it achieves strong generation quality (FID 0.029, R-Precision Top-1 0.686) under a unified robot-domain evaluator, while maintaining high motion safety and trajectory consistency. Real-world experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid demonstrate stable execution of diverse text commands with zero hardware fine-tuning.
SCDP: Learning Humanoid Locomotion from Partial Observations via Mixed-Observation Distillation
SCDP：通过混合观测提炼从部分观测中学习人形机器人的运动
从离线数据集中将类人机器人运动控制蒸馏为可部署策略仍是一项挑战，因为现有方法依赖于特权全身状态，而这需要复杂且往往不可靠的状态估计。我们提出传感器条件扩散策略（SCDP），仅使用车载传感器即可实现类人机器人运动，消除了对显式状态估计的需求。SCDP 通过混合观测训练将感知与监督解耦：扩散模型以传感器历史信息为条件，同时接受监督以预测特权的未来状态-动作轨迹，从而强制模型在部分可观测条件下推断运动动力学。我们进一步开发了受限去噪、上下文分布对齐和上下文感知注意力掩码，以促进模型内部的隐式状态估计并防止训练与部署的不匹配。我们在速度指令运动和运动参考跟踪任务上验证了 SCDP。在仿真中，SCDP 在速度控制上实现了接近完美的成功率（99-100%），在 AMASS 测试集上达到了 93% 的跟踪成功率，在仅使用车载传感器的情况下表现出与特权基准相当的性能。最后，我们以 50 Hz 的频率在真实的 G1 类人机器人上部署了训练好的策略，证明了在无需外部感知或状态估计的情况下，机器人能够实现鲁棒的现实运动。
Distilling humanoid locomotion control from offline datasets into deployable policies remains a challenge, as existing methods rely on privileged full-body states that require complex and often unreliable state estimation. We present Sensor-Conditioned Diffusion Policies (SCDP) that enables humanoid locomotion using only onboard sensors, eliminating the need for explicit state estimation. SCDP decouples sensing from supervision through mixed-observation training: diffusion model conditions on sensor histories while being supervised to predict privileged future state-action trajectories, enforcing the model to infer the motion dynamics under partial observability. We further develop restricted denoising, context distribution alignment, and context-aware attention masking to encourage implicit state estimation within the model and to prevent train-deploy mismatch. We validate SCDP on velocity-commanded locomotion and motion reference tracking tasks. In simulation, SCDP achieves near-perfect success on velocity control (99-100%) and 93% tracking success in AMASS test set, performing comparable to privileged baselines while using only onboard sensors. Finally, we deploy the trained policy on a real G1 humanoid at 50 Hz, demonstrating robust real robot locomotion without external sensing or state estimation.
HSImul3R: Physics-in-the-Loop Reconstruction of Simulation-Ready Human-Scene Interactions
HSImul3R：基于物理在环的仿真就绪型人机交互重建
我们提出 HSImul3R，这是一个用于从日常采集（包括稀疏视图图像和单目视频）中进行仿真就绪型人机交互（HSI）三维重建的统一框架。现有方法受困于“感知-仿真”鸿沟：视觉上合理的重建往往违反物理约束，导致其在物理引擎中表现不稳定，并在具身智能应用中失效。为了弥补这一差距，我们引入了一种基于物理规律的双向优化流水线，将物理仿真器作为主动监督者，共同精细化处理人体动力学和场景几何。在正向优化中，我们采用场景目标强化学习，在运动忠实度和接触稳定性双重监督下优化人体运动。在反向优化中，我们提出直接仿真奖励优化，利用仿真器对重力稳定性和交互成功率的反馈来精细化场景几何。我们还推出了 HSIBench，这是一个包含多样化物体和交互场景的新基准测试。大量实验证明，HSImul3R 首次生成了稳定、仿真就绪的 HSI 重建结果，并可直接部署到真实世界的类人机器人上。
We present HSImul3R, a unified framework for simulation-ready 3D reconstruction of human-scene interactions (HSI) from casual captures, including sparse-view images and monocular videos. Existing methods suffer from a perception-simulation gap: visually plausible reconstructions often violate physical constraints, leading to instability in physics engines and failure in embodied AI applications. To bridge this gap, we introduce a physically-grounded bi-directional optimization pipeline that treats the physics simulator as an active supervisor to jointly refine human dynamics and scene geometry. In the forward direction, we employ Scene-targeted Reinforcement Learning to optimize human motion under dual supervision of motion fidelity and contact stability. In the reverse direction, we propose Direct Simulation Reward Optimization, which leverages simulation feedback on gravitational stability and interaction success to refine scene geometry. We further present HSIBench, a new benchmark with diverse objects and interaction scenarios. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HSImul3R produces the first stable, simulation-ready HSI reconstructions and can be directly deployed to real-world humanoid robots.
ROSClaw: An OpenClaw ROS 2 Framework for Agentic Robot Control and Interaction
ROSClaw：一个用于智能体机器人控制和交互的 OpenClaw ROS 2 框架
基础模型能赋予机器人开放式推理、语言理解和自适应规划能力，但目前将模型连接到物理机器人仍需定制化的集成，将感知、执行与安全功能耦合在单一模型和平台上。我们提出 ROSClaw，一个与模型无关的执行层，它将 OpenClaw 智能体运行时与 ROS 2 集成，使任何基础模型都能通过以下方式感知、推理并作用于任何支持 ROS 的机器人：(i) 具有标准化可供性注入的动态能力发现，(ii) 多模态观测归一化，(iii) 配置化安全包络内的预执行动作验证，以及 (iv) 结构化审计日志。更换模型后端或机器人平台仅需更改配置；工具模式、安全执行和溯源日志保持不变。我们在三个平台（轮式、四足、类人）上部署了 ROSClaw，并使用了四个基础模型后端。在这种受控底层框架下，模型在策略外动作提议率上表现出高达 4.8 倍的差异（仅前沿模型间就有 3.4 倍），并对相同指令产生截然不同的物理行为。与 ROSA 进行的跨框架对等协议验证确认，执行层设计（而非仅仅是提示词表述）会显著影响任务完成度及安全行为，从而确立了 ROSClaw 既是实用的智能体机器人基础设施，也是具身智能领域可重复的测量工具。
Foundation models can endow robots with open-ended reasoning, language understanding, and adaptive planning, yet connecting a model to a physical robot today requires bespoke integration that couples perception, actuation, and safety to a single model and platform. We present ROSClaw, a model-agnostic executive layer that integrates the OpenClaw agent runtime with ROS 2, enabling any foundation model to perceive, reason about, and act on any ROS-enabled robot through (i) dynamic capability discovery with standardized affordance injection, (ii) multimodal observation normalization, (iii) pre-execution action validation within a configurable safety envelope, and (iv) structured audit logging. Swapping model backends or robot platforms is a configuration change; tool schemas, safety enforcement, and provenance logging remain invariant. We deploy ROSClaw on three platforms (wheeled, quadruped, humanoid) with four foundation-model backends. Under this controlled substrate, models exhibit up to 4.8 x differences in out-of-policy action proposal rates (3.4 x among frontier models alone) and produce qualitatively distinct physical behaviors from identical commands. A cross-framework parity protocol against ROSA confirms that executive-layer design, not just prompt wording, significantly affects both task completion and safety behavior, establishing ROSClaw as both practical agentic-robot infrastructure and a reproducible measurement instrument for embodied AI.
LooperMuscle: Fast and Stable Learning of Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking via Structured Mixture-of-Experts
LooperMuscle：通过结构化专家混合方法实现人形机器人全身追踪的快速稳定学习
FastSAC 风格的方法显著缩短了类人机器人的运动训练时间，但在全身跟踪任务中，其性能往往较 PPO 有明显下降。针对这一速度与性能之间的差距，我们引入了 LooperMuscle，这是一个组合式专家策略学习框架，在保持高训练效率的同时恢复了跟踪质量。LooperMuscle 结合了语义结构化的混合专家（MoE）策略网络、专家感知的分布增强式评论员（Critic），以及带有延迟课程调度的贡献路由回放机制。这三个组件形成了一个闭环训练回路：专家贡献引导数据路由，路由后的数据塑造价值学习，而价值梯度反过来精细化专家的专业化分工。实验表明，我们的方法在运动跟踪精度上大幅优于原生 FastSAC。虽然它的耗时远低于 PPO——FastSAC 训练约需 15 分钟但性能不佳，PPO 效果更强但需约 6 小时——而 LooperMuscle 仅需约 45 分钟即可达到与 PPO 相当的性能，为仿真到现实（sim-to-real）的迭代提供了实用的效率。
FastSAC-style methods significantly reduce humanoid motion training time but often suffer from notable performance degradation compared with PPO in whole-body tracking tasks. We target this speed–performance gap by introducing LooperMuscle, a composed expert policy learning framework that restores tracking quality while preserving high training efficiency. LooperMuscle combines a semantically structured mixture-of-experts actor, an expert-aware distributional critic, and contribution-routed replay with deferred curriculum scheduling. These three components form a closed training loop in which expert contributions guide data routing, routed data shape value learning, and value gradients in turn refine expert specialization. Empirically, our approach substantially outperforms vanilla FastSAC regarding motion tracking accuracy. While it requires far less wall-clock time than PPO: where FastSAC trains in about 15 minutes but underperforms, and PPO achieves stronger results but requires about 6 hours, LooperMuscle reaches comparable performance to PPO in roughly 45 minutes, and delivering practical efficiency for sim-to-real iteration.
SPARK: Skeleton-Parameter Aligned Retargeting on Humanoid Robots with Kinodynamic Trajectory Optimization
SPARK：基于运动学轨迹优化的类人机器人骨骼参数对齐重定向
人体运动为训练通用类人机器人控制策略提供了丰富的先验知识，但原始演示数据往往与机器人的运动学及动力学不匹配，限制了其直接应用。我们提出了一种两阶段流水线，用于从任务空间的人类数据生成自然且动力学可行的参考运动。首先，我们将人体运动转换为基于统一机器人描述格式（URDF）的骨架表示，并将其校准至目标类人机器人的尺寸。通过对齐底层骨架结构而非启发式地修改任务空间目标，这一步显著降低了逆运动学误差和调优工作量。其次，我们通过渐进式动力运动学轨迹优化（TO）来精炼重定向后的轨迹，优化过程分为三个阶段：运动学 TO、逆动力学、以及完整的动力运动学 TO，每一阶段都由前一阶段的解进行温启动。最终结果产出了动力学一致的状态轨迹和关节扭矩剖面，为基于学习的控制器提供了高质量的参考。骨架校准与动力运动学 TO 相结合，使得在不同的 Unitree G1 类人机器人平台上生成自然且物理一致的参考运动成为可能。
Human motion provides rich priors for training general-purpose humanoid control policies, but raw demonstrations are often incompatible with a robot's kinematics and dynamics, limiting their direct use. We present a two-stage pipeline for generating natural and dynamically feasible motion references from task-space human data. First, we convert human motion into a unified robot description format (URDF)-based skeleton representation and calibrate it to the target humanoid's dimensions. By aligning the underlying skeleton structure rather than heuristically modifying task-space targets, this step significantly reduces inverse kinematics error and tuning effort. Second, we refine the retargeted trajectories through progressive kinodynamic trajectory optimization (TO), solved in three stages: kinematic TO, inverse dynamics, and full kinodynamic TO, each warm-started from the previous solution. The final result yields dynamically consistent state trajectories and joint torque profiles, providing high-quality references for learning-based controllers. Together, skeleton calibration and kinodynamic TO enable the generation of natural, physically consistent motion references across diverse Unitree G1 humanoid platforms.
DiffusionAnything: End-to-End In-context Diffusion Learning for Unified Navigation and Pre-Grasp Motion
DiffusionAnything：面向统一导航和预抓取运动的端到端上下文扩散学习
直接从视觉高效地预测运动规划仍是机器人领域的一项基本挑战，通常规划需要显式的目标设定和任务特定设计。近期的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型虽然能直接从视觉输入推断动作，但需要海量的计算资源和广泛的训练数据，且在陌生场景中无法实现零样本（zero-shot）运行。我们提出一种统一的图像空间扩散策略，通过多尺度特征调制，仅需每项任务 5 分钟的自适应监督数据，即可处理米级导航和厘米级操作。该框架由三大核心创新驱动：(1) 针对任务模式、深度尺度和空间注意力的多尺度 FiLM 条件调节，使单一模型能够产生适配任务的行为；(2) 轨迹对齐的深度预测将度量 3D 推理集中在生成的路径点上；(3) 来自 AnyTraverse 的自监督注意力机制实现了无需视觉语言模型和深度传感器的目标导向推理。该模型仅依靠 RGB 输入运行（内存占用 2.0 GB，频率 10 Hz），在保持适用于车载部署的同时，实现了对新场景稳健的零样本泛化。我们将该方法部署在配备 RGB 相机的 Unitree G1 类人机器人上。
Efficiently predicting motion plans directly from vision remains a fundamental challenge in robotics, where planning typically requires explicit goal specification and task-specific design. Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models infer actions directly from visual input but demand massive computational resources, extensive training data, and fail zero-shot in novel scenes. We present a unified image-space diffusion policy handling both meter-scale navigation and centimeter-scale manipulation via multi-scale feature modulation, with only 5 minutes of self-supervised data per task. Three key innovations drive the framework: (1) Multi-scale FiLM conditioning on task mode, depth scale, and spatial attention enables task-appropriate behavior in a single model; (2) trajectory-aligned depth prediction focuses metric 3D reasoning along generated waypoints; (3) self-supervised attention from AnyTraverse enables goal-directed inference without vision-language models and depth sensors. Operating purely from RGB input (2.0 GB memory, 10 Hz), the model achieves robust zero-shot generalization to novel scenes while remaining suitable for onboard deployment.  We deploy our method on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot equipped with an RGB camera.
PCHC: Enabling Preference Conditioned Humanoid Control via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
PCHC：通过多目标强化学习实现基于偏好条件的人形机器人控制
类人机器人通常需要在相互冲突的目标之间取得平衡，例如在最大化运动速度的同时最小化能量消耗。虽然目前的强化学习（RL）方法已经能够掌握跌倒恢复和感知运动等复杂技能，但它们受限于固定的权重策略，往往只能生成单一的次优策略，而无法为复杂的多目标控制提供多样化的解决方案。在本文中，我们提出了一种利用多目标强化学习（MORL）实现偏好条件类人控制（PCHC）的新颖框架。与需要训练一系列策略来逼近帕累托前沿（Pareto front）的传统方法不同，我们的框架使单一的、以偏好为条件的策略能够展现出广泛且多样的行为。为了有效整合这些需求，我们引入了一种基于 Beta 分布的对齐机制，通过偏好向量来调节混合专家（MoE）模块。我们在两个具有代表性的类人机器人任务上验证了该方法。大量的仿真和真实世界实验表明，所提出的框架允许机器人根据输入的偏好条件，实时自适应地切换其目标优先级。该策略专门针对 Unitree G1 类人机器人进行了训练和部署。
Humanoid robots often need to balance competing objectives, such as maximizing speed while minimizing energy consumption. While current reinforcement learning (RL) methods can master complex skills like fall recovery and perceptive locomotion, they are constrained by fixed weighting strategies that produce a single suboptimal policy, rather than providing a diverse set of solutions for sophisticated multi-objective control. In this paper, we propose a novel framework leveraging Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) to achieve Preference-Conditioned Humanoid Control (PCHC). Unlike conventional methods that require training a series of policies to approximate the Pareto front, our framework enables a single, preference-conditioned policy to exhibit a wide spectrum of diverse behaviors. To effectively integrate these requirements, we introduce a Beta distribution-based alignment mechanism based on preference vectors modulating a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) module. We validated our approach on two representative humanoid tasks. Extensive simulations and real-world experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework allows the robot to adaptively shift its objective priorities in real-time based on the input preference condition. The policy is trained and deployed specifically for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot.
Learning Safe-Stoppability Monitors for Humanoid Robots
学习人形机器人的安全停止监控
紧急停止（E-stop）机制是机器人安全的行业标准。然而，对于类人机器人而言，突然切断电源本身就可能导致灾难性的故障；相反，紧急停止必须执行预定义的后备控制器，以保持平衡并将机器人引导至风险最小的状态。这提出了一个关键问题：类人机器人究竟能从哪些状态安全地执行此类停止动作？
在这项工作中，我们将类人机器人的紧急停止形式化为一个“策略相关的安全可停止性”（policy-dependent safe-stoppability）问题，并利用数据驱动的方法来刻画安全可停止包络线。我们引入了 PRISM（主动细化重要性采样可停止性监测器），这是一个仿真驱动的框架，用于学习状态级可停止性的神经预测器。PRISM 通过重要性采样迭代地精细化决策边界，从而实现对稀有但安全关键状态的有针对性探索。这种针对性探索在固定的仿真预算下显著提高了数据效率，同时减少了“错误安全”的预测。我们通过在真实的类人平台上部署预训练的监测器，进一步展示了从仿真到现实（sim-to-real）的迁移。结果表明，将安全性建模为策略相关的可停止性，能够实现主动安全监测，并支持 Unitree G1 类人机器人故障安全行为的可扩展认证。
Emergency stop (E-stop) mechanisms are the de facto standard for robot safety. However, for humanoid robots, abruptly cutting power can itself cause catastrophic failures; instead, an emergency stop must execute a predefined fallback controller that preserves balance and drives the robot toward a minimum-risk condition. This raises a critical question: from which states can a humanoid robot safely execute such a stop?
In this work, we formalize emergency stopping for humanoids as a policy-dependent safe-stoppability problem and use data-driven approaches to characterize the safe-stoppable envelope. We introduce PRISM (Proactive Refinement of Importance-sampled Stoppability Monitor), a simulation-driven framework that learns a neural predictor for state-level stoppability. PRISM iteratively refines the decision boundary using importance sampling, enabling targeted exploration of rare but safety-critical states. This targeted exploration significantly improves data efficiency while reducing false-safe predictions under a fixed simulation budget. We further demonstrate sim-to-real transfer by deploying the pretrained monitor on a real humanoid platform. Results show that modeling safety as policy-dependent stoppability enables proactive safety monitoring and supports scalable certification of fail-safe behaviors for Unitree G1 humanoid robots.
Cognition to Control - Multi-Agent Learning for Human-Humanoid Collaborative Transport
认知控制——面向人机协作运输的多智能体学习
有效的人机协作（HRC）需要将高层意图转化为接触稳定的全身运动，同时不断适应人类伙伴。许多视觉-语言-动作（VLA）系统学习从观测和指令到动作的端到端映射，但它们往往侧重于反应式（类似“系统 1”）行为，而对于如何将持续的、类似于“系统 2”的审慎决策与可靠、低延迟的连续控制相结合，则缺乏明确说明。这一差距在多智能体人机协作中尤为突出，因为长时程协调决策与物理执行必须在接触、可行性和安全约束下协同演化。
为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了“从认知到控制”（C2C），这是一个使“决策到控制”路径明确化的三层架构：(i) 基于 VLM（视觉语言模型）的锚定层，负责维护持久的场景指代并推断具身感知的可供性/约束；(ii) 审慎技能/协调层（系统 2 核心），通过去中心化多智能体强化学习（MARL），在人机耦合下优化长时程技能选择与序列，该过程被建模为一个以共享势能编码任务进度的马尔可夫势能博弈；(iii) 全身控制层，在强制执行运动学/动力学可行性和接触稳定性的同时，以高频执行所选技能。审慎层被实现为相对于名义控制器的残差策略，无需显式角色分配即可内化伙伴的动力学特性。在协作操作任务上的实验表明，该方法比单智能体和端到端基准具有更高的成功率和鲁棒性，并展现出稳定的协调性以及自发的领随（leader-follower）行为。为了弥合仿真到现实的差距，我们在 Unitree G1 类人机器人上进行了与人类伙伴协作的物理实验，并配备了动作捕捉（MoCap）系统。
Effective human-robot collaboration (HRC) requires translating high-level intent into contact-stable whole-body motion while continuously adapting to a human partner. Many vision-language-action (VLA) systems learn end-to-end mappings from observations and instructions to actions, but they often emphasize reactive (System 1-like) behavior and leave under-specified how sustained System 2-style deliberation can be integrated with reliable, low-latency continuous control. This gap is acute in multi-agent HRC, where long-horizon coordination decisions and physical execution must co-evolve under contact, feasibility, and safety constraints. We address this limitation with cognition-to-control (C2C), a three-layer hierarchy that makes the deliberation-to-control pathway explicit: (i) a VLM-based grounding layer that maintains persistent scene referents and infers embodiment-aware affordances/constraints; (ii) a deliberative skill/coordination layer-the System 2 core-that optimizes long-horizon skill choices and sequences under human-robot coupling via decentralized MARL cast as a Markov potential game with a shared potential encoding task progress; and (iii) a whole-body control layer that executes the selected skills at high frequency while enforcing kinematic/dynamic feasibility and contact stability. The deliberative layer is realized as a residual policy relative to a nominal controller, internalizing partner dynamics without explicit role assignment. Experiments on collaborative manipulation tasks show higher success and robustness than single-agent and end-to-end baselines, with stable coordination and emergent leader-follower behaviors. To bridge the sim-toreal gap, physical experiments are executed on a Unitree G1 humanoid
robot cooperating with a human partner, with a motion-capture (MoCap) system.
OmniTrack: General Motion Tracking via Physics-Consistent Reference
OmniTrack：基于物理一致性参考的通用运动跟踪
从丰富的运动数据中学习动作跟踪是实现类人机器人通用控制的基础任务，使其能够执行多样化的行为。然而，人类与机器人之间在形态和动力学上的差异，结合数据噪声，会导致参考运动中出现物理不可行的伪影（如漂浮和穿透现象）。在训练和执行过程中，这些伪影会在遵循不准确的参考运动与维持机器人稳定性之间产生冲突，阻碍了通用化动作跟踪策略的开发。为了应对这些挑战，我们推出了 OmniTrack，这是一个将物理可行性与通用动作跟踪明确解耦的通用跟踪框架。在第一阶段，特权通用策略通过仿真中的轨迹展开，生成严格遵守机器人动力学的物理合理运动。在第二阶段，训练通用控制策略来跟踪这些物理可行的运动，确保控制能稳定且连贯地迁移至真实机器人。实验表明，OmniTrack 提高了跟踪精度，并对未知动作表现出强大的泛化能力。在现实世界的测试中，OmniTrack 实现了长达一小时、持续且稳定的跟踪，包括空翻和侧空翻等复杂的特技动作。此外，我们证明了 OmniTrack 支持类人风格的稳定且动态的在线远程操作，彰显了其对不同用户输入的鲁棒性和适应性。在所有实验中，我们均使用 Unitree G1 类人机器人作为仿真和真实世界部署的统一平台。
Learning motion tracking from rich human motion data is a foundational task for achieving general control in humanoid robots, enabling them to perform diverse behaviors. However, discrepancies in morphology and dynamics between humans and robots, combined with data noise, introduce physically infeasible artifacts in reference motions, such as floating and penetration. During both training and execution, these artifacts create a conflict between following inaccurate reference motions and maintaining the robot's stability, hindering the development of a generalizable motion tracking policy. To address these challenges, we introduce OmniTrack, a general tracking framework that explicitly decouples physical feasibility from general motion tracking. In the first stage, a privileged generalist policy generates physically plausible motions that strictly adhere to the robot's dynamics via trajectory rollout in simulation. In the second stage, the general control policy is trained to track these physically feasible motions, ensuring stable and coherent control transfer to the real robot. Experiments show that OmniTrack improves tracking accuracy and demonstrates strong generalization to unseen motions. In real-world tests, OmniTrack achieves hour-long, consistent, and stable tracking, including complex acrobatic motions such as flips and cartwheels. Additionally, we show that OmniTrack supports human-style stable and dynamic online teleoperation, highlighting its robustness and adaptability to varying user inputs. In all experiments, we use the Unitree G1 humanoid as the unified platform for both simulation and real-world deployment.
Omnidirectional Humanoid Locomotion on Stairs via Unsafe Stepping Penalty and Sparse LiDAR Elevation Mapping
基于不安全步态惩罚和稀疏激光雷达高程映射的全向人形机器人楼梯移动
类人机器人具有多自由度和高重心的特征，本质上具有不稳定性。在楼梯上实现安全的运动，既需要全方位的地形感知，也需要可靠的落脚点选择。现有方法通常依赖前向深度摄像头，这会产生限制全方位移动能力的盲区。此外，稀疏的触地后不安全踏步惩罚会导致学习效率低且策略次优。为了实现安全的楼梯攀爬步态，本文引入了一个单阶段训练框架，其中包含一种密集的不安全踏步惩罚机制，当足部接近危险位置时，该机制可提供连续反馈。为了获得稳定可靠的高程图，我们构建了一个具有时空置信度衰减和自我保护区机制的滚动点云制图系统，从而生成时间一致的局部地图。这些地图通过边缘引导非对称 U-Net（EGAU）进一步精细化，该网络缓解了由于楼梯立面上的稀疏 LiDAR 回波导致的重建失真。仿真和真实机器人实验表明，所提方法在仿真楼梯地形上实现了接近 100% 的安全踏步率，同时在现实世界部署中保持了极高的安全踏步率。此外，它在复杂的户外地形上完成了连续长距离步行测试，证明了可靠的仿真到现实（sim-to-real）迁移能力和长期稳定性。本文使用的机器人平台是 Unitree G1 类人机器人，该机器人拥有 29 个自由度，能够执行复杂的全身运动。
Humanoid robots, characterized by numerous degrees of freedom and a high center of gravity, are inherently unstable. Safe omnidirectional locomotion on stairs requires both omnidirectional terrain perception and reliable foothold selection. Existing methods often rely on forward-facing depth cameras, which create blind zones that restrict omnidirectional mobility. Furthermore, sparse post-contact unsafe stepping penalties lead to low learning efficiency and suboptimal strategies. To realize safe stair-traversal gaits, this paper introduces a single-stage training framework incorporating a dense unsafe stepping penalty that provides continuous feedback as the foot approaches a hazardous placement. To obtain stable and reliable elevation maps, we build a rolling point-cloud mapping system with spatiotemporal confidence decay and a self-protection zone mechanism, producing temporally consistent local maps. These maps are further refined by an Edge-Guided Asymmetric U-Net (EGAU), which mitigates reconstruction distortion caused by sparse LiDAR returns on stair risers. Simulation and real-robot experiments show that the proposed method achieves a near-100\% safe stepping rate on stair terrains in simulation, while maintaining a remarkably high safe stepping rate in real-world deployments. Furthermore, it completes a continuous long-distance walking test on complex outdoor terrains, demonstrating reliable sim-to-real transfer and long-term stability. The robotic platform used in this paper is the Unitree G1 humanoid robot, which has 29 degrees of freedom and is capable of executing complex whole-body motions.
Fast SAM 3D Body: Accelerating SAM 3D Body for Real-Time Full-Body Human Mesh Recovery
快速SAM 3D人体模型：加速SAM 3D人体模型，实现实时全身人体网格恢复
SAM 3D Body (3DB) 在单目三维人体网格恢复方面达到了顶尖的准确度，但其每张图像数秒的推理延迟阻碍了实时应用。我们提出 Fast SAM 3D Body，这是一个无需训练的加速框架，通过重构 3DB 的推理路径实现了交互级速率。通过解耦串行空间依赖关系并应用架构感知剪枝，我们实现了并行化的多裁剪特征提取和精简的 Transformer 解码。此外，为了提取与现有类人机器人控制和策略学习框架兼容的关节级运动学（SMPL）参数，我们用直接前馈映射取代了迭代网格拟合，使这一特定转换加速了超过 10,000 倍。总体而言，我们的框架在保持同等重建精度的同时，实现了高达 10.9 倍的端到端加速，在 LSPET 等基准测试中甚至超过了 3DB。我们通过将 Fast SAM 3D Body 部署在一个纯视觉远程操作系统中证明了其效用；与依赖可穿戴惯性测量单元（IMU）的方法不同，该系统能够通过单个 RGB 流实现 Unitree G1 类人机器人的实时控制，并直接采集操作策略。
SAM 3D Body (3DB) achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in monocular 3D human mesh recovery, yet its inference latency of several seconds per image precludes real-time application. We present Fast SAM 3D Body, a training-free acceleration framework that reformulates the 3DB inference pathway to achieve interactive rates. By decoupling serial spatial dependencies and applying architecture-aware pruning, we enable parallelized multi-crop feature extraction and streamlined transformer decoding. Moreover, to extract the joint-level kinematics (SMPL) compatible with existing humanoid control and policy learning frameworks, we replace the iterative mesh fitting with a direct feedforward mapping, accelerating this specific conversion by over 10,000x. Overall, our framework delivers up to a 10.9x end-to-end speedup while maintaining on-par reconstruction fidelity, even surpassing 3DB on benchmarks such as LSPET. We demonstrate its utility by deploying Fast SAM 3D Body in a vision-only teleoperation system that-unlike methods reliant on wearable IMUs-enables real-time Unotree G1 humanoid control and the direct collection of manipulation policies from a single RGB stream.
Kimodo: Scaling Controllable Human Motion Generation
Kimodo：可扩展的可控人体运动生成
高质量的人体运动数据对于机器人、仿真和娱乐领域的应用正变得日益重要。近期的生成模型提供了一种潜在的数据来源，能够通过文本提示或姿态运动学约束等直观输入来合成人体运动。然而，公开动作捕捉（mocap）数据集的规模较小，限制了这些模型的运动质量、控制精度和泛化能力。在这项工作中，我们推出了 Kimodo，这是一个在 700 小时光学动作捕捉数据上训练而成的、具有表现力且可控的运动学运动扩散模型。我们的模型在生成高质量运动的同时，能够通过文本以及一套全面的运动学约束（包括全身关键帧、稀疏关节位置/旋转、2D 路径点和密集 2D 路径）进行轻松控制。这得益于精心设计的运动表示和两阶段去噪器架构，该架构通过分解根部和肢体预测来最大限度地减少运动伪影，同时允许灵活的约束调节。在大规模动捕数据集上的实验证明了关键设计决策的合理性，并分析了数据集规模和模型规模的扩展如何影响性能。
High-quality human motion data is becoming increasingly important for applications in robotics, simulation, and entertainment. Recent generative models offer a potential data source, enabling human motion synthesis through intuitive inputs like text prompts or kinematic constraints on poses. However, the small scale of public mocap datasets has limited the motion quality, control accuracy, and generalization of these models. In this work, we introduce Kimodo, an expressive and controllable kinematic motion diffusion model trained on 700 hours of optical motion capture data. Our model generates high-quality motions while being easily controlled through text and a comprehensive suite of kinematic constraints including full-body keyframes, sparse joint positions/rotations, 2D waypoints, and dense 2D paths. This is enabled through a carefully designed motion representation and two-stage denoiser architecture that decomposes root and body prediction to minimize motion artifacts while allowing for flexible constraint conditioning. Experiments on the large-scale mocap dataset justify key design decisions and analyze how the scaling of dataset size and model size affect performance.
Heracles: Bridging Precise Tracking and Generative Synthesis for General Humanoid Control
赫拉克勒斯：连接精确追踪和生成式合成，实现通用人形机器人控制
实现通用类人机器人控制，需要在精确执行指令运动与应对不可预测环境扰动所需的灵活、类人自适应能力之间取得微妙平衡。目前的通用控制器主要将运动控制建模为硬性的参考跟踪问题。虽然在常规条件下有效，但这些跟踪器在严重干扰下往往表现出脆弱且非类人化的失败模式，缺乏人类运动控制固有的生成式自适应性。为了克服这一局限性，我们提出了 Heracles，这是一种新颖的状态条件扩散中间件，架起了精确运动跟踪与生成式合成之间的桥梁。Heracles 并不依赖于硬性跟踪范式或复杂的显式模式切换，而是作为高层参考运动与底层物理跟踪器之间的中介层运行。通过以机器人的实时状态为条件，该扩散模型能隐式地调整其行为：当状态与参考运动紧密对齐时，它近似于恒等映射，从而保持零样本（zero-shot）跟踪的保真度；相反，当遇到显著的状态偏差时，它会无缝转换为生成式合成器，产生自然且类人的恢复轨迹。我们的框架证明，将生成式先验集成到控制回路中，不仅显著增强了应对极端扰动的鲁棒性，还将类人机器人控制从僵化的跟踪范式提升为开放式的生成式通用架构。所有实验均在 Unitree G1 类人机器人平台上完成，该机器人是一款全尺寸双足机器人，身高约 1.32 米，总质量约为 35 千克。
Achieving general-purpose humanoid control requires a delicate balance between the precise execution of commanded motions and the flexible, anthropomorphic adaptability needed to recover from unpredictable environmental perturbations. Current general controllers predominantly formulate motion control as a rigid reference-tracking problem. While effective in nominal conditions, these trackers often exhibit brittle, non-anthropomorphic failure modes under severe disturbances, lacking the generative adaptability inherent to human motor control. To overcome this limitation, we propose Heracles, a novel state-conditioned diffusion middleware that bridges precise motion tracking and generative synthesis. Rather than relying on rigid tracking paradigms or complex explicit mode-switching, Heracles operates as an intermediary layer between high-level reference motions and low-level physics trackers. By conditioning on the robot's real-time state, the diffusion model implicitly adapts its behavior: it approximates an identity map when the state closely aligns with the reference, preserving zero-shot tracking fidelity. Conversely, when encountering significant state deviations, it seamlessly transitions into a generative synthesizer to produce natural, anthropomorphic recovery trajectories. Our framework demonstrates that integrating generative priors into the control loop not only significantly enhances robustness against extreme perturbations but also elevates humanoid control from a rigid tracking paradigm to an open-ended, generative general-purpose architecture. All experiments are conducted on the Unitree G1 humanoid platform, a full-size bipedal robot standing approximately 1.32 m tall with a total mass of roughly 35 kg.
DRIVE-Nav: Directional Reasoning, Inspection, and Verification for Efficient Open-Vocabulary Navigation
DRIVE-Nav：用于高效开放词汇导航的方向推理、检查和验证
开阔词汇目标导航（OVON）要求具身智能体在未知环境中定位由语言指定的目标。现有的零样本（zero-shot）方法通常在不完全观测下对密集的边界点（frontier points）进行推理，导致路径选择不稳定、重复访问以及不必要的动作开销。我们提出 DRIVE-Nav，这是一个结构化框架，它围绕持久的方向（persistent directions）而非原始边界来组织探索。通过更完整地检查所遇到的方向，并将后续决策限制在前方 240 度视野范围内仍相关的方向上，DRIVE-Nav 减少了冗余访问并提高了路径效率。该框架从加权快速行进法（FMM）路径中提取并跟踪候选方向，维护具有代表性的视图以进行语义检查，并将视觉-语言引导的提示词富化与跨帧验证相结合，以提高定位的可靠性。在 HM3D-OVON、HM3Dv2 和 MP3D 上的实验证明了其强大的综合性能和持续的效率提升。在 HM3D-OVON 上，DRIVE-Nav 实现了 50.2% 的成功率（SR）和 32.6% 的成功路径长度加权（SPL），较此前最优方法分别提升了 1.9% 的 SR 和 5.6% 的 SPL。它在 HM3Dv2 和 MP3D 上也取得了最佳的 SPL，并成功迁移至 Unitree G1 物理类人机器人。真实世界的部署也证明了其有效性。
Open-Vocabulary Object Navigation (OVON) requires an embodied agent to locate a language-specified target in unknown environments. Existing zero-shot methods often reason over dense frontier points under incomplete observations, causing unstable route selection, repeated revisits, and unnecessary action overhead. We present DRIVE-Nav, a structured framework that organizes exploration around persistent directions rather than raw frontiers. By inspecting encountered directions more completely and restricting subsequent decisions to still-relevant directions within a forward 240 degree view range, DRIVE-Nav reduces redundant revisits and improves path efficiency. The framework extracts and tracks directional candidates from weighted Fast Marching Method (FMM) paths, maintains representative views for semantic inspection, and combines vision-language-guided prompt enrichment with cross-frame verification to improve grounding reliability. Experiments on HM3D-OVON, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate strong overall performance and consistent efficiency gains. On HM3D-OVON, DRIVE-Nav achieves 50.2% SR and 32.6% SPL, improving the previous best method by 1.9% SR and 5.6% SPL. It also delivers the best SPL on HM3Dv2 and MP3D and transfers to a physical Unitree G1 humanoid robot. Real-world deployment also demonstrates its effectiveness.
X-Loco: Towards Generalist Humanoid Locomotion Control via Synergetic Policy Distillation
虽然近期在类人机器人的单项技能（如站立运动、跌倒恢复和全身协调）方面取得了显著进展，但由于涉及多样的动力学特性和相互冲突的控制目标，训练一个能够精通所有这些技能的单一策略仍然具有挑战性。为了解决这一问题，我们推出了 X-Loco，这是一个用于训练基于视觉的通用类人运动策略的框架。X-Loco 首先训练多个专家（specialist）策略，并采用一种带有“案例自适应专家选择机制”的协同策略蒸馏方法，动态地利用多个专家策略来引导一个基于视觉的学生（student）策略。这种设计使学生策略能够获得广泛的运动技能，涵盖从跌倒恢复到地形穿越及全身协调的各种能力。据我们所知，X-Loco 是首个证明基于视觉的类人运动控制可以同时整合站立运动、全身协调和跌倒恢复的框架，且该框架仅在速度指令下运行，不依赖于参考运动。实验结果表明，X-Loco 在跌倒恢复和地形穿越等任务中表现优异。消融实验进一步强调，我们的框架有效地利用了专家经验并提升了学习效率。我们将 X-Loco 部署在 Unitree G1 机器人上，展示了其在多种地形和挑战性场景下的卓越性能与稳定性。
While recent advances have demonstrated strong performance in individual humanoid skills such as upright locomotion, fall recovery and whole-body coordination, learning a single policy that masters all these skills remains challenging due to the diverse dynamics and conflicting control objectives involved. To address this, we introduce X-Loco, a framework for training a vision-based generalist humanoid locomotion policy. X-Loco trains multiple oracle specialist policies and adopts a synergetic policy distillation with a case-adaptive specialist selection mechanism, which dynamically leverages multiple specialist policies to guide a vision-based student policy. This design enables the student to acquire a broad spectrum of locomotion skills, ranging from fall recovery to terrain traversal and whole-body coordination skills. To the best of our knowledge, X-Loco is the first framework to demonstrate vision-based humanoid locomotion that jointly integrates upright locomotion, whole-body coordination and fall recovery, while operating solely under velocity commands without relying on reference motions. Experimental results show that X-Loco achieves superior performance, demonstrated by tasks such as fall recovery and terrain traversal. Ablation studies further highlight that our framework effectively leverages specialist expertise and enhances learning efficiency. We deploy X-Loco on the Unitree G1 robot, demonstrating its superior performance and
stability across diverse terrains and challenging scenarios
Interaction-Aware Whole-Body Control for Compliant Object Transport
用于顺应性物体运输的交互感知全身控制
对于在非结构化环境中协作搬运物体而言，由于强烈的、随时间变化的交互作用力可能使以跟踪为核心的全身控制变得不可靠，尤其是在近距离接触的支撑任务中，这对比类人助手机器人提出了巨大挑战。本文提出了一种受生物启发、面向交互的全身控制（IO-WBC）框架，其功能类似于“人工小脑”——一种能够将上层（技能级）指令转化为触连状态下稳定且物理一致的全身行为的自适应运动智能体。该工作在结构上将上肢交互执行与下肢支撑控制分离，使机器人能够在紧密耦合的“机器人-物体”系统中平衡自身，同时调节力交换。轨迹优化参考生成器（RG）提供运动学先验，而强化学习（RL）策略则负责主导机器人在重载交互和扰动下的身体反应。该策略在仿真中通过随机化的负载质量/惯性及外部扰动进行训练，并利用非对称教生蒸馏（teacher-student distillation）进行部署，使得学生策略在运行时仅依赖本体感受历史数据。大量实验证明，即使在精确速度跟踪变得不可行的情况下，IO-WBC 仍能保持稳定的全身行为和物理交互，从而实现在广泛场景下的柔顺物体搬运。训练过程在 Isaac Lab [30] 中完成，物理实验则是在 Unitree G1 机器人上进行的，由机器人与人类伙伴协作并依赖动作捕捉系统完成。
Cooperative object transport in unstructured environments remains challenging for assistive humanoids because strong, time-varying interaction forces can make tracking-centric whole-body control unreliable, especially in close-contact support tasks. This paper proposes a bio-inspired, interaction-oriented whole-body control (IO-WBC) that functions as an artificial cerebellum - an adaptive motor agent that translates upstream (skill-level) commands into stable, physically consistent whole-body behavior under contact. This work structurally separates upper-body interaction execution from lower-body support control, enabling the robot to maintain balance while shaping force exchange in a tightly coupled robot-object system. A trajectory-optimized reference generator (RG) provides a kinematic prior, while a reinforcement learning (RL) policy governs body responses under heavy-load interactions and disturbances. The policy is trained in simulation with randomized payload mass/inertia and external perturbations, and deployed via asymmetric teacher-student distillation so that the student relies only on proprioceptive histories at runtime. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IO-WBC maintains stable whole-body behavior and physical interaction even when precise velocity tracking becomes infeasible, enabling compliant object transport across a wide range of scenarios. The training is performed in the Isaac Lab [30], and the physical experiments are conducted
on a Unitree G1 robot cooperating with a human partner with reliance on a motioncapture
Cross-Hand Latent Representation for Vision-Language-Action Models
视觉-语言-动作模型的交叉手部潜在表示
灵巧操作对于现实世界中的机器人自主性至关重要，它镜像了人类手部协调在日常活动中的核心作用。人类依赖丰富的多模态感知——视觉、声音和语言引导的意图——来执行灵巧动作，这激发了开发基于视觉、语言条件的机器人操作系统。然而，为灵巧操作训练可靠的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型需要跨多种机器人手的海量演示数据。此外，随着新的灵巧具身设备迅速出现，为每种设备单独收集数据变得昂贵且不切实际，因此产生了对可扩展跨具身学习的需求。我们推出了 XL-VLA，这是一个集成了统一潜动作空间（latent action space）的视觉-语言-动作框架，该空间由多种灵巧手共享。这种具身不变的潜空间可直接插入标准的 VLA 架构中，从而实现无缝的跨具身训练，并高效复用现有及新收集的数据。实验结果表明，XL-VLA 的表现持续优于在原始关节空间运行的基准 VLA 模型，证明其是实现可扩展跨具身灵巧操作的有效解决方案。我们使用了一个双臂 7 自由度 xArm 和一个配备各种机器人手的 Unitree G1 类人机器人进行实验。

This is especially challenging for humanoids because locomotion and manipulation are tightly coupled through stance, reachability, and balance. We present a humanoid agent framework that turns VLM plans into verifiable task programs and closes the loop with multi object 3D geometric supervision. Using SAM3 and RGB-D, we ground all task relevant entities in 3D, estimate object centroids and extents, and evaluate predicates over stable frames to obtain condition level diagnostics. PhyGile: Physics-Prefix Guided Motion Generation for Agile General Humanoid Motion Tracking
PhyGile：基于物理前缀的敏捷通用人形机器人运动跟踪运动生成
Humanoid robots are expected to execute agile and expressive whole-body motions in real-world settings. Existing text-to-motion generation models are predominantly trained on captured human motion datasets, whose priors assume human biomechanics, actuation, mass distribution, and contact strategies. When such motions are directly retargeted to humanoid robots, the resulting trajectories may satisfy geometric constraints (e.g., joint limits and pose continuity) and appear kinematically reasonable. However, they frequently violate the physical feasibility required for real-world execution. To address these issues, we present PhyGile, a unified framework that closes the loop between robot-native motion generation and General Motion Tracking (GMT). PhyGile performs physics-prefix-guided robot-native motion generation at inference time, directly generating robot-native motions in a 262-dimensional skeletal space with physics-guided prefixes, thereby eliminating inference-time retargeting artifacts and reducing generation-execution discrepancies. Before physics-prefix adaptation, we train the GMT controller with a curriculum-based mixture-of-experts scheme, followed by post-training on unlabeled motion data to improve robustness over large-scale robot motions. During physics-prefix adaptation, the GMT controller is further fine-tuned with generated objectives under physics-derived prefixes, enabling agile and stable execution of complex motions on real robots. Extensive offline and real-robot experiments demonstrate that PhyGile expands the frontier of text-driven humanoid control, enabling stable tracking of agile, highly difficult whole-body motions that go well beyond walking and low-dynamic motions typically achieved by prior methods.
类人机器人被期望在现实场景中执行敏捷且富有表现力的全身运动。现有的文本生成运动模型主要在人体动捕数据集上训练，其先验假设符合人体生物力学、驱动方式、质量分布和触地策略。当这些运动直接重定向到类人机器人时，生成的轨迹虽然可能满足几何约束（如关节限制和姿态连续性）且在运动学上看起来合理，但往往违反现实执行所需的物理可行性。为了解决这些问题，我们提出了 PhyGile，这是一个在机器人原生运动生成与通用运动跟踪（GMT）之间实现闭环的统一框架。PhyGile 在推理时执行物理前缀引导的机器人原生运动生成，直接在具有物理引导前缀的 262 维骨骼空间中生成机器人原生运动，从而消除了推理时的重定向伪影并减少了生成与执行之间的差异。在物理前缀自适应之前，我们使用基于课程学习的混合专家方案训练 GMT 控制器，随后在无标签运动数据上进行后训练，以提高在大规模机器人运动中的鲁棒性。在物理前缀自适应期间，GMT 控制器在物理衍生前缀下针对生成目标进行进一步微调，从而在真实机器人上实现复杂运动的敏捷稳定执行。广泛的离线和实机实验表明，PhyGile 拓展了文本驱动类人控制的前沿，能够稳定跟踪敏捷、高难度的全身运动，这些运动远超以往方法通常实现的行走和低动态运动。
